# obsidian-pdf-exporter

> obsidian-pdf-exporter (`ope`) is a command-line tool that exports a folder of an Obsidian vault to one PDF. It handles wiki links, embeds, callouts, Mermaid, math, footnotes, Bases and community plugin syntax (Dataview, Meta Bind, Excalidraw, draw.io, citations), makes redline PDFs between two git commits, and styles the PDF with CSS templates. Install with `uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter && ope setup --yes`.

- `ope` and `obsidian-pdf-exporter` are the same command. `ope <command> --help` is authoritative.
- The PDF is laid out by WeasyPrint from HTML written by pandoc. Templates are CSS Paged Media.
- A Claude Code plugin with an agent skill lives in the repository: `/plugin marketplace add Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter`.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/

# obsidian-pdf-exporter

![obsidian-pdf-exporter](img/banner.png)

<p class="ope-tagline">Export a folder of Obsidian notes to one PDF, with wiki links, embeds, callouts, Mermaid, math and community plugin syntax. Runs locally or in CI.</p>

## What it does

-   :material-folder-file-outline: __A folder becomes a document__

    Every folder is a section, every folder note its text. Headings are numbered and listed in a table of contents.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Folder structure](obsidian/structure.md)

-   :simple-obsidian: __Obsidian syntax__

    Wiki links, embeds of notes, headings and blocks, callouts, highlights, comments, tasks, footnotes, Mermaid, math and Bases.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Obsidian features](obsidian/index.md)

-   :material-puzzle-outline: __Community plugins__

    Dataview queries, Meta Bind views, Excalidraw drawings, citations, Block Link Plus ranges and draw.io diagrams render to static content.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Plugins](plugins/index.md)

-   :material-file-compare: __Redline__

    A tracked-changes PDF between two git commits, for reviews and audits.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Redline](redline.md)

-   :material-palette-outline: __Templates__

    CSS, running header and footer and page rules. A letterhead or a new footer is a folder with a few files.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Templates and styling](templating/index.md)

-   :material-robot-outline: __Ready for AI agents__

    A Claude Code plugin with a skill, plus `llms.txt` for any other agent.

    [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Use with AI agents](agents.md)

## From note to PDF

Each feature page shows the Markdown next to the rendered PDF. For example a callout:

Markdown:

````markdown
> [!tip] A custom title
> The title replaces the type name.

> [!faq]- Foldable callouts are always shown open
> The `+` and `-` markers are accepted.

> [!warning] Nested callouts
> Outer text.
>
> > [!info] Inner callout
> > Inner text.

> [!note] Lazy continuation
A line without `>` still belongs to the callout,
as in Obsidian.

| Status | Note |
| ------ | ---- |
| Done   | > [!success] Inline callout in a cell |
````

PDF:

![Callouts in the PDF](img/features/callouts.png)

## Get going in a minute

=== "Linux / macOS"

    ```bash
    curl -LsSf uvx.sh/obsidian-pdf-exporter/install.sh | sh && ope setup --yes
    ```

=== "Windows"

    ```powershell
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://uvx.sh/obsidian-pdf-exporter/install.ps1 | iex; ope setup --yes"
    ```

Then export a folder of your vault:

```bash
ope export ./MyVault/Handbook --title "Team handbook"
```

The PDF lands in `./.export/Team handbook.pdf`. Next: the [quick start](getting-started/quick-start.md).

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/intro/

# Introduction

obsidian-pdf-exporter (`ope`) turns a folder of an Obsidian vault into one PDF. It runs on the command line, so the same export works on a laptop and in a CI pipeline. It does not need Obsidian itself.

## Who it is for

- Teams who write handbooks, specifications or procedures in Obsidian and hand out PDFs.
- Projects that keep their docs in git and want a PDF per release, built by CI.
- Reviews that need a tracked-changes PDF between two versions of the docs.

## How it works

An export runs in three layers, the same layers the code is split into:

1. Markdown dialect. Pandoc reads the notes as Markdown with a fixed set of extensions. See [Markdown](markdown/index.md).
2. Obsidian core syntax. A list of small steps rewrites what Obsidian adds to Markdown: wiki links, embeds, callouts, comments and more. See [Obsidian](obsidian/index.md).
3. Community plugins. Plugin support modules render syntax of community plugins such as Dataview, Meta Bind, Excalidraw or citations. See [Plugins](plugins/index.md).

Pandoc then writes HTML, and [WeasyPrint](https://weasyprint.org/) lays out the PDF with the CSS of a [template](templating/index.md).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Vault folder] --> B[Core steps and plugins]
    B --> C[pandoc: HTML]
    C --> D[Template CSS]
    D --> E[WeasyPrint: PDF]
```

## What it is not

- Not an Obsidian plugin. It runs outside Obsidian and reads the files on disk.
- Not a pixel copy of the Obsidian reading view. The PDF is styled by its template, and some interactive features (folding, input fields, buttons) have no PDF form.
- Not a full Dataview engine. It renders a subset of DQL, see [Dataview](plugins/dataview.md).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/redline/

# Redline

`ope redline` builds a PDF that shows what changed in a folder between two git commits: inserted text in green, removed text in red and struck through. It is meant for reviews, approvals and audits of documents kept in git.

```bash
cd MyVault                     # must run inside the git repository
ope redline ./Handbook --from-commit v3.0.0 --to-commit HEAD
```

The PDF is written to `./.export/<title>_redline.pdf`. All options are in the [CLI reference](reference/cli.md#redline).

## Example

Before (commit 1):

````markdown
## Scope

This policy applies to all laptops.

## Rules

- Lock the screen when you leave the desk.
- Install updates once a month.
- Report a lost device within one day.

## Old exceptions

Test devices are exempt.
````

After (commit 2):

````markdown
## Scope

This policy applies to all laptops and phones.

## Rules

- Lock the screen when you leave the desk.
- Install updates once a week.
- Report a lost device within one day.
- Use the password manager for all accounts.
````

PDF:

![Redline PDF with inserted and removed text](img/features/redline.png)

## How changes are shown

- A block that changed a little (similar enough to the old one) shows word-level changes inline, as `<ins>` and `<del>`.
- A block that is new, or changed so much that the old and new text have little in common, is shown as a removed block followed by an inserted block (`.redline-del` and `.redline-ins`).
- Removed headings are shown as bold text, so they do not go into the table of contents or the numbering.
- Both commits are exported with the same steps and plugins, so embeds, Dataview tables and Meta Bind values are compared as they appear in the PDF.

The subtitle and the version label show the two short hashes, such as `Redline: 1a2b3c4 -> 5d6e7f8`. `--subtitle` replaces the subtitle.

## Template

`redline` uses the built-in `redline` template. It looks like `default` and adds the styles for the changes. A custom template for redlines styles these selectors:

| Selector | Marks |
| -------- | ----- |
| `ins`, `del` | Word-level insertions and removals. |
| `.redline-ins`, `.redline-del` | Inserted and removed blocks. |

See the [CSS reference](templating/css-reference.md#redline).

## In CI

The checkout needs the history of both commits:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
- run: ope redline ./Handbook --from-commit "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}" -o redline.pdf
```

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/agents/

# Use with AI agents

ope is a command-line tool with plain flags, real exit codes and text output, so coding agents can run it like any other CLI. Two things help them use it well: a skill that explains how, and a short index of these docs.

## Claude Code plugin

The repository is a Claude Code plugin marketplace with one plugin. The plugin holds the `obsidian-pdf-exporter` skill: how to install ope when it is missing, export, redline, templates, debugging, and how to check the PDF with `pdftotext` and `pdftoppm`.

In Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter
/plugin install obsidian-pdf-exporter@obsidian-pdf-exporter
```

Claude Code 2.1.275 and later can do both in one step:

```text
/plugin install obsidian-pdf-exporter --marketplace Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter
```

From a shell:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter
claude plugin install obsidian-pdf-exporter@obsidian-pdf-exporter
claude plugin details obsidian-pdf-exporter   # shows the skill
```

Updates arrive with `/plugin marketplace update`. The skill loads when a task is about exporting notes to PDF. It can also be called directly as `/obsidian-pdf-exporter:obsidian-pdf-exporter`.

## Copy the skill by hand

The skill is a plain [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io/) folder, [`skills/obsidian-pdf-exporter/`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/tree/main/skills/obsidian-pdf-exporter). Copy it into the skills folder of your agent:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter /tmp/ope

# Claude Code, for all projects
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r /tmp/ope/skills/obsidian-pdf-exporter ~/.claude/skills/

# Claude Code, for one project (commit it to share with the team)
mkdir -p .claude/skills && cp -r /tmp/ope/skills/obsidian-pdf-exporter .claude/skills/
```

Other agents that read Agent Skills use their own folder, such as `.github/skills/` or `.agents/skills/`. Tools like `npx skills add Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter` fetch the same folder.

## Other agents: llms.txt

These docs publish an index for language models, following [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/):

- [`llms.txt`](https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/llms.txt): a short description and a link to every page.
- [`llms-full.txt`](https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/llms-full.txt): the text of all pages in one file.

Point an agent without skill support at one of them, for example in its rules file:

```markdown
## PDF export

Export Obsidian notes to PDF with `ope` (obsidian-pdf-exporter). Install it with
`uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter && ope setup --yes`. Docs for agents:
https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/llms.txt
```

## Working on ope itself

The repository has an [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/AGENTS.md) for agents that change the code: setup, checks, the layers of the pipeline, where new syntax goes, and how to rebuild the docs and screenshots.

## Example prompt

```text
Export the folder "Handbook" of my vault to PDF with the title "Team handbook"
and version 2.0.0. Use a template with our logo (logo.svg in the repo root) at the
top right of every page and "Page X of Y" in the footer. Check the PDF and tell me
about any warnings or raw Obsidian syntax left in it.
```

With the skill, the agent installs ope if needed, builds a template folder from a copy of `default.css` with the logo as a running element, runs the export, and checks the result with `pdftotext` and the rendered pages.

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.10 or higher
- Git
- `uv` (Python package manager)
- `jq` (for JSON processing)

### Install jq

```bash
sudo apt-get install jq
```

### Install `uv`

Following the [uv installation guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation):

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Add shell completion (optional):

```bash
echo 'eval "$(uv generate-shell-completion bash)"' >> ~/.bashrc
```

### Project Setup

1. **Fork and Clone the Repository**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter.git
   cd obsidian-pdf-exporter
   ```

2. **Install Dependencies**

   ```bash
   uv sync --all-groups
   ```

   This will:
   - Create a virtual environment
   - Install all dependencies (including development dependencies via dependency groups)
   - Install the project in editable mode

3. **Verify Installation**

   ```bash
   uv run obsidian-pdf-exporter --help
   uv run ope --help
   ```

## Development Workflow

### Running the Application

```bash
# Run with uv (recommended)
uv run obsidian-pdf-exporter [commands]
uv run ope [commands]

# Or activate the virtual environment
source .venv/bin/activate
obsidian-pdf-exporter [commands]
```

### Adding Dependencies

```bash
# Add runtime dependency
uv add package-name

# Add development dependency (to dev group)
uv add --group dev package-name

# Add to custom dependency group
uv add --group group-name package-name
```

### Updating Dependencies

```bash
# Update all dependencies
uv sync --upgrade

# Update specific dependency
uv sync --upgrade-package package-name
```

## Architecture

An export reads a folder of notes and turns it into one PDF. The work is
split into three layers. Each layer has one place where its parts are
listed.

1. Markdown dialect ([`core/dialect.py`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/core/dialect.py)).
   The pandoc reader extensions and pandoc arguments. The base is pandoc's
   `markdown` reader with `raw_html` and `lists_without_preceding_blankline`
   on and `raw_tex` off. Steps add what they need, for example `mark` for
   highlights, `hard_line_breaks` for line breaks or `--mathml` for math.
2. Obsidian core syntax ([`core/steps/`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/tree/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/core/steps/)).
   Every piece of syntax that Obsidian itself supports is a small step:
   frontmatter, comments, Bases, PDF embeds, embeds, block IDs, callouts, heading links, wiki
   links, image captions, headings, warnings about plugin code blocks,
   highlights, line breaks, tasks, math, footnotes, Mermaid, landscape
   diagrams, SVG images and table fixes. All steps are listed in
   `CORE_STEPS` in [`core/steps/__init__.py`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/core/steps/__init__.py).
3. Community plugins ([`plugins/`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/tree/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/)).
   Support for syntax from community Obsidian plugins and other tools:
   Folder Notes, Dataview, Excalidraw, Meta Bind, Block Link Plus, draw.io
   and pandoc citations. Plugins
   are found through an entry point, listed by `list-plugins` and can be
   turned off with `--disable-plugin`. They run inside the `plugins` step
   of layer 2.

```text
obsidian_pdf_exporter/
├── core/
│   ├── exporter.py         # export and redline: tree → markdown → HTML → PDF
│   ├── assemble.py         # runs the markdown hooks on every page
│   ├── pipeline.py         # the loops over the steps, one per stage
│   ├── dialect.py          # layer 1: pandoc reader extensions and arguments
│   ├── pandoc.py           # runs pandoc with a dialect
│   ├── steps/              # layer 2: one module per piece of core syntax
│   │   ├── __init__.py     # CORE_STEPS, the ordered list of steps
│   │   ├── base.py         # Step, PageContext, DocumentContext
│   │   ├── frontmatter.py, plugins.py, comments.py, bases.py, embeds.py, block_ids.py,
│   │   ├── callouts.py, heading_links.py, wiki_links.py, image_captions.py,
│   │   ├── headings.py, code_blocks.py, highlights.py, line_breaks.py, tasks.py, math.py,
│   │   ├── footnotes.py, landscape.py, pdf_embeds.py,
│   │   └── mermaid.py, svg_images.py, tables.py, base_css.py
│   ├── bases/              # Bases: expression parser, evaluator and views
│   ├── code.py             # outside_code: keeps fenced and inline code as written
│   └── embeds.py, callouts.py, wiki_links.py, mermaid.py, ...  # the work behind the steps
├── plugins/                # layer 3
│   ├── base.py             # ObsidianPlugin, PluginContext, DocumentContext
│   ├── registry.py         # entry-point + runtime discovery
│   ├── folder_notes/, dataview/, meta_bind/
│   ├── excalidraw/         # Excalidraw drawings drawn as SVG
│   ├── block_link_plus/    # ![[Note#^id-id]] ranges
│   ├── drawio/             # draw.io SVG labels
│   └── citations/          # [@key] citations with pandoc citeproc
└── templates/              # PDF templates (CSS, header, footer)
```

### Stages

A step overrides the hooks it needs:

| Hook                       | Runs on                                  | Order            |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------|------------------|
| `process_markdown`         | each page, and embedded notes if `embedded = True` | `priority`       |
| `process_document`         | the assembled markdown of the whole document | `priority`   |
| `reader_extensions`, `pandoc_args` | builds the dialect for pandoc    | `priority`       |
| `process_html`             | the HTML that pandoc wrote               | `html_priority` (defaults to `priority`) |

An export runs them in this order: the markdown hooks on every page, the
document hooks, the template's `process_markdown`, pandoc, the HTML hooks,
the template's `process_html`, and WeasyPrint. With `--debug`, the build
folder keeps `assembled.md` (what pandoc reads) and `final.html` (what
WeasyPrint reads).

The order of the markdown steps matters. For example, `embeds` runs after
`html_comments`, so an embed inside an HTML comment is not expanded. It
runs before `block_ids`, so the block IDs in embedded text are removed
too. `bracket_links` runs after `wiki_links`, so real wiki links are
already resolved. The table in the docstring of
[`core/steps/__init__.py`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/core/steps/__init__.py)
gives the reason for each position.

Embedded notes (`![[Note]]`) run through the steps marked `embedded`
(`plugins`, `html_comments`, `bases`, `pdf_embeds`, `embeds`, `footnotes` and `wiki_links`) with the context of
the embedded note, so links and images resolve from its folder. The
embedded text then becomes part of the page and passes the remaining steps.

### Adding a core syntax step

Add a step only for syntax that Obsidian supports without a community
plugin. Everything else is a plugin (see below).

1. Put the step in a new module under `core/steps/`. Keep it thin and
   put larger parsing code in a module of its own under `core/`:

   ```python
   from obsidian_pdf_exporter.core.steps.base import PageContext
   from obsidian_pdf_exporter.core.steps.base import Step

   class SubscriptStep(Step):
       name = "subscript"
       description = "Render ~sub~ as subscript"
       priority = 115  # after image_captions (110), before title_heading (120)

       def reader_extensions(self, context):
           return ("subscript",)

       def process_markdown(self, content: str, context: PageContext) -> str:
           return content
   ```

2. Add the class to `CORE_STEPS` in `core/steps/__init__.py`, at the
   position of its priority, and to the table in the module docstring.
3. Leave code alone. Obsidian shows fenced code blocks and inline code
   as written, so wrap the rewrite in `outside_code` from
   [`core/code.py`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/core/code.py).
4. Never drop content silently. When the step sees syntax it can not
   render, it keeps it in a simple form and reports it with
   `context.warn(...)`, which prints a line starting with `Warning:`.
5. Add tests. [`test_steps.py`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/tests/unit/test_steps.py) checks the
   order of all steps, so update the expected lists there.
6. Describe the syntax in the docs (see [Documentation](#documentation)).

## Adding support for an Obsidian plugin

Obsidian plugins (Dataview, Meta Bind, Tasks, Templater, Excalidraw …)
introduce non-core syntax into markdown notes. To make those notes export
cleanly, the project carries one **plugin support module** per Obsidian
plugin. They all live under [`obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/tree/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/),
one subpackage per plugin, so contributors have an obvious place to add a
new one.

### File layout

```text
obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/
├── base.py          # ObsidianPlugin base class + PluginContext, DocumentContext
├── registry.py      # entry-point + runtime discovery
├── dataview/
│   ├── __init__.py  # re-exports DataviewPlugin
│   ├── plugin.py    # the plugin class (thin)
│   └── engine.py    # DQL parser + renderer (heavy lifting)
├── drawio/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── plugin.py
│   └── svg.py       # draw.io label conversion
└── meta_bind/
    ├── __init__.py
    └── plugin.py
```

Keep the plugin class itself thin and put any non-trivial parsing,
indexing or rendering in sibling modules so it stays easy to test in
isolation. The Dataview package is the canonical example.

The currently bundled plugins are:

| Plugin         | What it covers                                           |
|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `folder_notes` | Map ``Folder/Folder.md`` onto its containing folder      |
| `dataview`     | Render Dataview DQL ``TABLE`` / ``LIST`` queries         |
| `excalidraw`   | Turn embedded Excalidraw drawings into images            |
| `meta_bind`    | Resolve Meta Bind ``VIEW`` widgets, strip INPUT/BUTTON   |
| `block_link_plus` | Resolve ``![[Note#^id-id]]`` range embeds             |
| `drawio`       | Turn draw.io HTML labels in SVG images into SVG text     |
| `citations`    | Render ``[@key]`` citations with ``pandoc --citeproc``   |

### Walkthrough — adding a new plugin

Suppose you want to add support for the **Tasks** plugin so its
``- [ ] do thing 📅 2026-05-10`` syntax renders as a clean checkbox list.

#### 1. Create the package

```text
obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/tasks/
├── __init__.py
└── plugin.py
```

`__init__.py`:

```python
"""Support for the Obsidian `Tasks` plugin."""

from obsidian_pdf_exporter.plugins.tasks.plugin import TasksPlugin

__all__ = ["TasksPlugin"]
```

#### 2. Implement the plugin class

Every plugin subclasses
[`ObsidianPlugin`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/base.py) and overrides
``process_markdown(content, context)``. ``context`` is a
``PluginContext`` carrying the page's vault root, page folder,
frontmatter, and the user's ``--option key=value`` settings.

`plugin.py`:

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import re

from obsidian_pdf_exporter.plugins.base import ObsidianPlugin
from obsidian_pdf_exporter.plugins.base import PluginContext

_TASK_LINE = re.compile(r"^(\s*-\s\[)([ x/\-])(\]\s.+)$", re.MULTILINE)

class TasksPlugin(ObsidianPlugin):
    """Strip Tasks emoji-suffixes (📅, ⏫, …) and normalise checkbox state."""

    name = "tasks"
    description = "Render Tasks-plugin checkboxes without emoji metadata"
    priority = 50  # runs after dataview (10) and meta_bind (20)

    def process_markdown(self, content: str, context: PluginContext) -> str:
        # Drop the trailing emoji-tagged metadata that Tasks renders.
        content = re.sub(r"\s+[⏩-⏺✅❌\U0001F4C5][^\n]*", "", content)
        return _TASK_LINE.sub(lambda m: m.group(1) + m.group(2).lower() + m.group(3), content)
```

The pipeline guarantees:

- Frontmatter is already parsed and stripped before your plugin runs.
- Plugins run **before** embeds, callouts, wiki link resolution and image
  promotion, so anything your plugin produces flows through the rest of
  the pipeline like authored markdown would.
- Plugins also run on the content of embedded notes, with the context of
  the embedded note.
- ``context.vault_root`` may be ``None`` for ad-hoc exports outside a
  git repository — gracefully no-op in that case if you need vault-wide
  data (see the Dataview plugin for the pattern).

#### 3. Register it via an entry point

Add the new class to ``pyproject.toml``:

```toml
[project.entry-points."obsidian_pdf_exporter.obsidian_plugins"]
dataview = "obsidian_pdf_exporter.plugins.dataview:DataviewPlugin"
meta_bind = "obsidian_pdf_exporter.plugins.meta_bind:MetaBindPlugin"
tasks = "obsidian_pdf_exporter.plugins.tasks:TasksPlugin"
```

Re-install the project in editable mode so the entry point is picked up:

```bash
uv pip install -e .
```

Verify:

```bash
uv run obsidian-pdf-exporter list-plugins
```

#### 4. Add unit tests

Drop a file in `tests/unit/` that imports your plugin directly and feeds
it a few representative markdown snippets. Mirror the style in
[`test_plugins.py`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/tests/unit/test_plugins.py).

#### 5. Document it

Add a page under `docs/plugins/`, an example note under `examples/` and
its screenshot (see [Documentation](#documentation)), and list the plugin
in the table above.

### Plugin priority

`priority` is an integer — lower runs earlier. The built-ins use:

| Plugin         | Priority |
|----------------|----------|
| `folder_notes` | 5        |
| `dataview`     | 10       |
| `excalidraw`   | 15       |
| `meta_bind`    | 20       |
| `block_link_plus` | 30    |
| `drawio`       | 40       |
| `citations`    | 50       |

Pick a value that respects your dependencies (e.g. if your plugin
substitutes frontmatter fields like Meta Bind, run after Dataview so any
tables it generated are visible).

### Hooks

A plugin can override any of these methods on
[`ObsidianPlugin`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/base.py). All have
no-op defaults so you only implement what you need. A plugin that only
implements `process_markdown` keeps working:

| Hook                 | Stage                                | Used by                        |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| `find_folder_note`   | Tree building                        | `folder_notes`                 |
| `process_markdown`   | Per-page markdown rewrite            | `dataview`, `meta_bind`, `excalidraw` |
| `extract_block`      | Resolving `![[Note#^id]]` embeds     | `block_link_plus`              |
| `process_document`   | Assembled markdown of the whole document | `citations`                |
| `reader_extensions`, `pandoc_args` | Building the pandoc call (after `process_document`) | `citations` |
| `process_svg`        | Inlining SVG images into the HTML    | `drawio`                       |
| `process_html`       | HTML of the whole document           | none yet                       |

`find_folder_note(folder)` returns the markdown file that represents a
folder (or ``None``). Plugins are consulted in priority order; the
first non-None result wins. Use this when the Obsidian plugin you are
mirroring affects which file is the "page" for a folder. Examples:

- The bundled `folder_notes` plugin returns ``Folder/Folder.md``.
- A `readme_folder_notes` plugin could return ``Folder/README.md``.
- A frontmatter-driven plugin could return whichever file in the
  folder has ``folder-note: true``.

`process_markdown(content, context)` runs after frontmatter has been
stripped and before callouts / wiki links / image promotion. The
``context`` dataclass exposes ``vault_root``, ``page_folder``,
``frontmatter`` and the user's ``--option key=value`` settings.

`extract_block(body, block_id)` returns the text that `![[Note#^block_id]]`
selects in the note body, or ``None``. Plugins are asked in priority
order before core looks for a block marked ``^block_id``.

`process_document(markdown, context)` gets the assembled markdown of the
whole document, after the markdown hook ran on every page. The plugin can
then return pandoc reader extensions and arguments from
`reader_extensions(context)` and `pandoc_args(context)`, for example
`--citeproc` when it found citations.

`process_svg(svg, context)` rewrites each SVG image while it is inlined
into the HTML. `process_html(html, context)` gets the HTML of the whole
document after the core HTML steps and before the template. Both get a
``DocumentContext`` with the build folder, the options, the export
metadata and the template.

### Disabling and configuring plugins

Users can opt out of a single plugin per export with
``--disable-plugin <name>`` (repeatable). Free-form configuration is
forwarded through the existing ``--option key=value`` CLI flag and
exposed to every hook via ``context.options``.

### Third-party plugins

Plugins are not required to live in this repository. Anyone can publish
a separate Python distribution that registers a plugin under the same
``obsidian_pdf_exporter.obsidian_plugins`` entry point group; installing
it makes it instantly available to ``obsidian-pdf-exporter`` without
code changes here. Only add a plugin to this repository if it covers a
broadly used Obsidian plugin and is not better maintained as a separate
package.

## Adding a PDF template

PDF appearance (layout, header, footer, colour palette) is provided by
**templates**, a separate extension point that lives next to the plugin
system but is not the same thing. Templates plug into rendering, plugins
plug into markdown.

End users do **not** need to touch this repository to ship a custom
look. [Templates and styling](https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templating/) in the docs covers the
no-Python options — drop-in CSS file, template directory with a
`template.yaml` manifest, or a named directory under
`~/.config/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templates/`. Reach for the steps below
only when your template needs to mutate markdown or HTML (i.e. requires
Python code).

Templates that ship inside this project live under
[`obsidian_pdf_exporter/templates/builtin/`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/tree/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/templates/builtin/);
each one ships a ``Template`` subclass plus its CSS file. To add one:

1. Drop a new package next to ``default`` and ``redline``.
2. Subclass
   [`Template`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/templates/base.py) and override
   ``get_css()`` (return CSS source) and optionally ``decorations(ctx)``
   to inject running header/footer HTML and ``@page`` rules.
3. Register the class under the ``obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates``
   entry point group in ``pyproject.toml`` and reinstall.

Branded or company-specific templates should usually be published as a
separate distribution rather than added here.

## Testing

We use `pytest` for testing. Tests are located in the `tests/` directory.

### Running Tests

```bash
# Run all tests
uv run pytest

# Run tests with verbose output
uv run pytest -v

# Run specific test file
uv run pytest tests/test_basic.py

# Run specific test
uv run pytest tests/test_basic.py::test_package_imports
```

### Writing Tests

1. **Create test files** in the `tests/` directory with the prefix `test_`
2. **Follow naming conventions**: `test_*.py` files, `test_*` functions
3. **Use descriptive test names** that explain what is being tested
4. **Add docstrings** to explain complex test scenarios

Example test structure:

```python
def test_feature_description() -> None:
    """Test that the feature works as expected."""
    # Arrange
    input_data = "test input"

    # Act
    result = function_under_test(input_data)

    # Assert
    assert result == expected_output
```

## Code Quality

### Linting with Ruff

We use `ruff` for Python linting and code formatting.

```bash
# Check code quality
uv run ruff check

# Auto-fix issues where possible
uv run ruff check --fix

# Check specific files or directories
uv run ruff check obsidian_pdf_exporter/
uv run ruff check tests/
```

### Code Style Guidelines

- **Line length**: Maximum 100 characters
- **Docstring style**: Google docstring convention
- **Import formatting**: One import per line (enforced by ruff)
- **Type hints**: Use type annotations for new code

### Pre-commit Workflow

Before committing:

1. **Run linting**: `uv run ruff check`
2. **Run tests**: `uv run pytest`
3. **Fix any issues** before committing

## Documentation

The documentation site is built with [Zensical](https://zensical.org/)
from `mkdocs.yml` and `docs/`, and published to GitHub Pages by
`.github/workflows/docs.yml` on every push to `main`.

```bash
uv sync --group docs
uv run zensical serve            # live preview on http://localhost:8000
uv run zensical build --strict   # what CI runs
```

Generated content:

- `docs/reference/cli.md` comes from the Typer app. Run
  `uv run python scripts/gen_cli_docs.py` after changing a command or
  flag. CI fails when the page is out of date.
- `docs/img/features/*.png` and `docs/img/templates/*.png` are rendered
  from the example vault in `examples/`. Each folder there (not starting
  with `_`) is one example and becomes `docs/img/features/<folder>.png`.
  Run `uv run python scripts/render_examples.py [name ...]` after a change
  that affects the output. It needs `pdftoppm` (poppler) and Node.js for
  Mermaid. Commit the images.
- `docs/llms.txt` and `docs/llms-full.txt` come from the pages. Run
  `uv run python scripts/gen_llms_txt.py` after adding or renaming a page.
  CI fails when they are out of date.

A feature page shows the example source next to its image with the
`ope-example` block, see any page under `docs/obsidian/`. The source is
included with `--8<-- "examples/<name>/<name>.md"`, so it cannot drift
from the note that was rendered.

# Installation

ope is a Python package with two native dependencies: the Pango text stack that WeasyPrint uses, and pandoc. The installer below puts the CLI in place, and `ope setup` installs the native parts.

## Install the CLI

=== "Linux / macOS"

    ```bash
    curl -LsSf uvx.sh/obsidian-pdf-exporter/install.sh | sh && ope setup --yes
    ```

=== "Windows"

    ```powershell
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://uvx.sh/obsidian-pdf-exporter/install.ps1 | iex; ope setup --yes"
    ```

=== "uv"

    ```bash
    uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter
    ope setup --yes

    # or run it once without installing
    uvx obsidian-pdf-exporter --help
    ```

=== "pip"

    ```bash
    pip install obsidian-pdf-exporter
    ope setup --yes
    ```

The installer script installs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) if needed and runs `uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter`, so the CLI lives in its own environment. A pinned version uses the version in the URL:

```bash
curl -LsSf uvx.sh/obsidian-pdf-exporter/0.5.1/install.sh | sh
```

`ope` and `obsidian-pdf-exporter` are the same command.

## Native dependencies

- [WeasyPrint](https://weasyprint.org/) needs Pango, GLib, HarfBuzz (with `harfbuzz-subset`) and Fontconfig. Cairo is not needed. The package lists follow [WeasyPrint's first steps](https://doc.courtbouillon.org/weasyprint/stable/first_steps.html).
- [Pandoc](https://pandoc.org/) converts Markdown to HTML. If it is missing, `ope setup` downloads it from the official pandoc release with `pypandoc`.

```bash
ope setup           # install what is missing, asks first
ope setup --yes     # same, without asking (for CI)
ope setup --check   # report only, exit 1 if something is missing
```

`setup` only runs the package manager of your platform:

| OS | What `setup` runs when libraries are missing | Notes |
| -- | -------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| Debian / Ubuntu | `sudo apt-get install -y libpango-1.0-0 libpangoft2-1.0-0 libharfbuzz0b libharfbuzz-subset0 ...` | Same list as the WeasyPrint docs. |
| Fedora | `sudo dnf install -y pango` | Pulls GLib, HarfBuzz and Fontconfig. |
| Arch | `sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm pango` | |
| openSUSE | `sudo zypper install -y pango` | |
| Alpine | `sudo apk add pango fontconfig` | |
| macOS | `brew install pango` | Needs [Homebrew](https://brew.sh). Without it, `setup` prints the install link and exits with 1. |
| Windows | `winget install --id tschoonj.GTKForWindows --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements` | The GTK3 runtime. An [Inkscape](https://inkscape.org/) install also brings GTK. |

When WeasyPrint still cannot find the libraries, set `OBSIDIAN_PDF_GTK_PATH` to the folders that hold them, separated by `os.pathsep`.

## Optional tools

| Tool | Needed for |
| ---- | ---------- |
| git | [Redline](../redline.md), the version label from the commit hash, and the vault root for Dataview. |
| Node.js (`npx`) or `mmdc` | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md) diagrams. Without it, Mermaid blocks stay code blocks. |

## In CI

A GitHub Actions job that exports a folder and keeps the PDF:

```yaml
jobs:
  pdf:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0   # full history for redline and the version label
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
      - run: uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter
      - run: ope setup --yes
      - run: ope export ./Handbook --title "Team handbook" --version "${{ github.ref_name }}" -o handbook.pdf
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: handbook
          path: handbook.pdf
```

## Check the install

```bash
ope --version
ope setup --check
ope list-templates
ope list-plugins
```

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/getting-started/quick-start/

# Quick start

## Export a folder

```bash
ope export ./MyVault/Handbook
```

The PDF is written to `./.export/Handbook.pdf`. The folder name is the title. Every subfolder becomes a section, see [Folder structure](../obsidian/structure.md).

## Title, version and output

```bash
ope export ./MyVault/Handbook \
  --title "Team handbook" --subtitle "How we work" \
  --version 3.1.0 --date 2026-05-07 \
  --output ./out/handbook.pdf
```

The title and subtitle go into the title block and the running header. The version and date go into the footer of the `default` template. Without `--version`, a folder inside a git repository shows the short commit hash.

## Only some chapters

```bash
ope export ./MyVault/Handbook --include "Chapter A" --include "Chapter B"
ope export ./MyVault/Handbook --exclude "Drafts" --no-toc
```

`--include` and `--exclude` take names of the top-level subfolders.

## A different look

```bash
ope list-templates
ope export ./MyVault/Handbook --template ./my-template/
```

A template is a CSS file or a folder with CSS, header and footer. See [Templates and styling](../templating/index.md).

## Settings for features

`-O key=value` passes settings to the steps, plugins and the template:

```bash
ope export ./MyVault/Handbook -O mermaid.theme=neutral -O tables.landscape=off
ope export ./MyVault/Handbook --disable-plugin dataview
```

All keys are listed in the [CLI reference](../reference/cli.md#options-for-o-keyvalue).

## Tracked changes

```bash
cd MyVault
ope redline ./Handbook --from-commit v3.0.0 --to-commit HEAD
```

See [Redline](../redline.md).

## When something looks wrong

```bash
ope export ./MyVault/Handbook --debug
```

`--debug` keeps the build folder next to the PDF. `assembled.md` is what pandoc reads, `final.html` is what WeasyPrint lays out. See [Debugging](../templating/debugging.md).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/reference/cli/

# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_docs.py from the Typer app. Do not edit by hand. -->

# CLI reference

`ope` and `obsidian-pdf-exporter` are the same command. Run `ope --help` or `ope <command> --help` for the same information in the terminal.

```text
ope [--version] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Command | Summary |
| ------- | ------- |
| [`version`](#version) | Print the installed version. |
| [`setup`](#setup) | Install missing system dependencies (Pango/HarfBuzz/Fontconfig, pandoc). |
| [`list-templates`](#list-templates) | List all known PDF templates (built-in, packaged, user-config, runtime). |
| [`list-plugins`](#list-plugins) | List all installed Obsidian-plugin support modules (built-in + third-party). |
| [`export`](#export) | Export an Obsidian-format folder tree to a single PDF file. |
| [`redline`](#redline) | Generate a redline (tracked-changes) PDF between two git commits. |

## `version`

Print the installed version.

```text
ope version
```

Prints the installed version. `ope --version` does the same.

```bash
ope version
```

## `setup`

Install missing system dependencies (Pango/HarfBuzz/Fontconfig, pandoc).

```text
ope setup [OPTIONS]
```

Installs missing native dependencies (Pango, HarfBuzz, Fontconfig and pandoc) with the package manager of the platform. See [Installation](../getting-started/installation.md).

| Option | Description | Default |
| ------ | ----------- | ------- |
| `--check` | Diagnose only — do not install anything (exit 1 if something is missing) | off |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Skip the confirmation prompt | off |

```bash
ope setup --check   # report only
ope setup --yes     # install without asking
```

## `list-templates`

List all known PDF templates (built-in, packaged, user-config, runtime).

```text
ope list-templates
```

Prints every known template with its source: built-in, packaged entry point, user-config folder or registered at runtime. See [Templates](../templating/index.md).

```bash
ope list-templates
```

## `list-plugins`

List all installed Obsidian-plugin support modules (built-in + third-party).

```text
ope list-plugins
```

Prints every installed plugin support module, sorted by priority. See [Plugins](../plugins/index.md).

```bash
ope list-plugins
```

## `export`

Export an Obsidian-format folder tree to a single PDF file.

```text
ope export ROOT [OPTIONS]
```

Builds one PDF from a vault folder. Git is not required. When the folder is in a git repository and `--version` is not set, the short commit hash is shown as the version label. See [Folder structure](../obsidian/structure.md) for how the folder becomes sections.

| Argument | Description |
| -------- | ----------- |
| `ROOT` | Path to the vault folder to export (required) |

| Option | Description | Default |
| ------ | ----------- | ------- |
| `-T NAME\|PATH`, `--template NAME\|PATH` | Template name (see `list-templates`) or path to a custom template (.css file or directory with template.yaml) | `default` |
| `-o PATH`, `--output PATH` | Output PDF path (default: ./.export/&lt;title&gt;.pdf) |  |
| `-t TEXT`, `--title TEXT` | Document title (default: folder name) |  |
| `--subtitle TEXT` | Document subtitle |  |
| `-v TEXT`, `--version TEXT` | Document version (e.g. 3.1.0) |  |
| `-d YYYY-MM-DD`, `--date YYYY-MM-DD` | Document date (YYYY-MM-DD, default: today) |  |
| `--include NAME` | Only include these subfolder names. Repeatable. |  |
| `--exclude NAME` | Exclude these subfolder names. Repeatable. |  |
| `-O KEY=VALUE`, `--option KEY=VALUE` | Pass key=value options to plugins / template (repeatable) |  |
| `--disable-plugin NAME` | Skip the named Obsidian plugin (repeatable; see `list-plugins`) |  |
| `--toc/--no-toc` | Include a table of contents at the start of the document | `--toc` |
| `--debug` | Keep the intermediate build directory for inspection | off |

```bash
ope export ./Vault/Handbook \
  --title "Team handbook" --subtitle "How we work" \
  --version 3.1.0 --date 2026-05-07 \
  --include "Chapter A" --include "Chapter B" \
  --disable-plugin meta_bind \
  -O mermaid.theme=neutral -O tables.landscape=off
```

## `redline`

Generate a redline (tracked-changes) PDF between two git commits.

```text
ope redline ROOT [OPTIONS]
```

Builds a tracked-changes PDF between two git commits. Must run inside the git repository that holds `ROOT`. See [Redline](../redline.md).

| Argument | Description |
| -------- | ----------- |
| `ROOT` | Path to the vault folder to export (required) |

| Option | Description | Default |
| ------ | ----------- | ------- |
| `--from-commit REF` | Older git commit ref (baseline) | required |
| `--to-commit REF` | Newer git commit ref (default: HEAD) | `HEAD` |
| `-T NAME\|PATH`, `--template NAME\|PATH` | Template name (default: redline) or path to a custom template (.css file or directory with template.yaml) | `redline` |
| `-o PATH`, `--output PATH` | Output PDF path (default: ./.export/&lt;title&gt;_redline.pdf) |  |
| `-t TEXT`, `--title TEXT` | Document title (default: folder name) |  |
| `--subtitle TEXT` | Document subtitle |  |
| `-O KEY=VALUE`, `--option KEY=VALUE` | Pass key=value options to plugins / template (repeatable) |  |
| `--disable-plugin NAME` | Skip the named Obsidian plugin (repeatable; see `list-plugins`) |  |
| `--toc/--no-toc` | Include a table of contents at the start of the document | `--toc` |
| `--debug` | Keep the intermediate build directory for inspection | off |

```bash
ope redline ./Vault/Handbook --from-commit v3.0.0 --to-commit HEAD
```

## Options for `-O key=value`

`-O` (`--option`) passes free-form settings to the core steps, the plugins and
the template. These keys are read by ope itself:

| Key | Values | Default | Described in |
| --- | ------ | ------- | ------------ |
| `line_breaks` | `hard`, `soft` | from `.obsidian/app.json` | [Line breaks](../obsidian/line-breaks.md) |
| `tables.landscape` | `auto`, `on`, `off` | `auto` | [Tables](../markdown/tables.md#wide-tables) |
| `tables.landscape_min_cols` | number | `6` | [Tables](../markdown/tables.md#wide-tables) |
| `mermaid` | `off` | on | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md) |
| `mermaid.format` | `svg`, `png` | `svg` | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#options) |
| `mermaid.scale` | number | `3` | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#options) |
| `mermaid.config` | path to JSON | none | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#options) |
| `mermaid.theme` | Mermaid theme | none | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#options) |
| `mermaid.cli` | command | auto | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#options) |
| `mermaid.puppeteer_config` | path | none | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#options) |
| `mermaid.trim` | `on`, `off` | `on` | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#options) |
| `mermaid.max_height` | CSS length | none | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#options) |
| `mermaid.landscape` | `on`, `off` | `on` | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#wide-diagrams) |
| `mermaid.landscape_ratio` | number | `1.4` | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#wide-diagrams) |
| `mermaid.landscape_min_font` | points | `7` | [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md#wide-diagrams) |
| `footnotes` | `page`, `end` | `page` | [Footnotes](../markdown/footnotes.md) |
| `pdf_embeds` | `pages`, `link` | `pages` | [Embeds](../obsidian/embeds.md#pdf) |
| `pdf_embeds.max_pages` | number | `10` | [Embeds](../obsidian/embeds.md#pdf) |
| `pdf_embeds.dpi` | number | `150` | [Embeds](../obsidian/embeds.md#pdf) |
| `citations` | `off` | on | [Citations](../plugins/citations.md#options) |
| `citations.bibliography` | paths, separated by `,` | auto | [Citations](../plugins/citations.md#bibliography) |
| `citations.csl` | path to a CSL style | Chicago author-date | [Citations](../plugins/citations.md#options) |
| `citations.title` | text | `References` | [Citations](../plugins/citations.md#options) |
| `excalidraw.auto_export` | `on`, `off` | `on` | [Excalidraw](../plugins/excalidraw.md#auto-export-files-first) |

Third-party plugins and templates can read any other key. By convention a
plugin uses `<plugin>.<key>` and a template `<template>.<key>`.

## Environment variables

| Name | Purpose |
| ---- | ------- |
| `OBSIDIAN_PDF_GTK_PATH` | Extra folders, separated by `os.pathsep`, that are searched for the GTK and Pango libraries (Windows and macOS). |
| `OBSIDIAN_PDF_EXPORTER_TEMPLATES_DIR` | Folder scanned for named user templates. Default: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templates`, or `~/.config/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templates`. |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Moves the default user templates folder. |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | Success. |
| `1` | The export failed, `setup --check` found a missing dependency, an install command failed, or `redline` ran outside a git repository. |
| `2` | Bad arguments, for example an unknown template or a malformed `-O` value. |
| `130` | Aborted at the `setup` confirmation prompt. |

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/markdown/

# Markdown

The first layer of an export is the Markdown dialect: the pandoc reader and its extensions. It is defined in one place, [`core/dialect.py`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/core/dialect.py).

## The dialect

The base is pandoc's `markdown` reader with these settings:

| Setting | Why |
| ------- | --- |
| `+raw_html` | HTML in notes is passed through, as in Obsidian. |
| `+lists_without_preceding_blankline` | A list may start right after a paragraph, as in Obsidian. |
| `-raw_tex` | Text like `A\B` stays as written. |
| `--number-sections` | Headings are numbered. |
| `--columns=100000` | Table columns are sized by their content, not by the dash count of the source. |
| `--toc --toc-depth=4` | The table of contents, unless `--no-toc` is set. |

The core syntax steps add what they need on top, for example `mark` for [highlights](../obsidian/highlights-comments.md) and `hard_line_breaks` for [line breaks](../obsidian/line-breaks.md). Math is rendered by a step of its own, see [Math](math.md).

Anything else pandoc's Markdown reader understands works too, for example definition lists, fenced divs (`::: {.note}`) and attributes on headings (`## Title {#my-id}`). Obsidian does not show those, so they are not covered here.

## Pages in this section

| Page | Covers |
| ---- | ------ |
| [Headings and text](text.md) | Headings, emphasis, horizontal rules |
| [Lists](lists.md) | Bullet, numbered and nested lists |
| [Tables](tables.md) | Alignment, column widths, wide tables on landscape pages |
| [Code blocks](code.md) | Fenced code with syntax highlighting |
| [Block quotes](quotes.md) | Quotes and nested quotes |
| [Footnotes](footnotes.md) | Reference and inline footnotes |
| [Links and images](links-images.md) | Markdown links, URLs and images |
| [Inline HTML](html.md) | HTML tags inside notes |
| [Math](math.md) | Inline and display LaTeX math |

The screenshots are made from the notes in [`examples/`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/tree/main/examples) with the `default` template. The title block, header and footer are hidden so only the feature shows. [Contributing](../contributing.md#documentation) explains how to rebuild them.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/markdown/text/

# Headings and text

## Headings

Headings are numbered and go into the table of contents (down to level 4). The headings of a page nest under the page's own heading, so a note's `##` becomes a level below its section. See [Folder structure](../obsidian/structure.md).

Markdown:

````markdown
## Overview

Text under a level 2 heading.

### Details

#### Fine print

Headings are numbered and listed in the table of contents.
````

PDF:

![Numbered headings in the PDF](../img/features/headings.png)

A page that starts with `###` (it skips a level) is closed up, so section numbers never contain a `0`.

## Emphasis

Markdown:

````markdown
Text can be *italic*, **bold**, ***bold and italic*** or ~~struck through~~.

Underscores work too: _italic_ and __bold__.

Inline code looks like `ope export ./Notes`.
````

PDF:

![Italic, bold and struck-through text](../img/features/emphasis.png)

## Horizontal rules

`---`, `***` and `___` on their own line draw a thin line.

Markdown:

````markdown
Text above the rule.

---

Text between two rules.

***

Text below the rule.
````

PDF:

![Horizontal rules](../img/features/horizontal-rules.png)

The CSS for all of this is in the [CSS reference](../templating/css-reference.md).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/markdown/lists/

# Lists

Markdown:

````markdown
Shopping list:
- Apples
- Bread
    - Whole grain
    - Rye
- Milk

1. Open the vault
2. Run the export
    1. Pick a template
    2. Set a title
3. Share the PDF

5. A list can start at any number
6. and keeps counting
````

PDF:

![Bullet, numbered and nested lists](../img/features/lists.png)

- Nested lists are indented by four spaces or one tab.
- A list can follow a paragraph without a blank line in between, as in Obsidian.
- A numbered list keeps its start number.
- Task lists (`- [ ]`) are covered in [Tasks](../obsidian/tasks.md).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/markdown/tables/

# Tables

## Alignment

Colons in the separator row set the alignment of a column. Cells can hold inline formatting, code and links.

Markdown:

````markdown
| Left aligned | Centered | Right aligned |
| :----------- | :------: | ------------: |
| Apples       |   Red    |          1.20 |
| Bananas      |  Yellow  |          0.80 |
| Grapes       |  Green   |          3.50 |

Cells can hold **formatting**, `code` and [[#Left aligned|links]].
````

PDF:

![Table with left, centered and right aligned columns](../img/features/tables.png)

## Column widths

Columns are sized by their content, as in Obsidian, also for tables with long source lines. A table with set widths (an HTML `<colgroup>`) keeps their ratio. A very narrow column, such as an image column, is widened to half of an equal share, at most 20%.

Header rows repeat when a table breaks across pages. Rows do not split.

## Wide tables

A table that needs more width than a portrait page has goes to its own landscape page. The text after it continues on a new portrait page.

Markdown:

````markdown
A table that does not fit the page width moves to its own landscape page.

| ID | Requirement | Rationale | Owner | Status | Verification | Notes |
| -- | ----------- | --------- | ----- | ------ | ------------ | ----- |
| R-1 | The export runs without network access | Builds run in closed networks | Build team | Done | Automated test on an offline runner | None |
| R-2 | Every page shows the document version | Readers can tell revisions apart | Docs team | Open | Review of the footer on each page | Needs template change |

The text continues on the next portrait page.
````

PDF:

![A wide table on a landscape page between two portrait pages](../img/features/wide-tables.png)

A table goes to landscape when it has at least 6 columns and its content does not fit. The width is estimated from the text: each column counts with its longest cell (up to 25 characters, longer text wraps) or its longest word, which cannot wrap. An image counts as a full cell. A table of short values, such as keys and numbers, stays in the text.

| Option | Effect | Default |
| ------ | ------ | ------- |
| `-O tables.landscape=auto\|on\|off` | `auto` uses the estimate. `on` turns every table with enough columns. `off` keeps all tables portrait. | `auto` |
| `-O tables.landscape_min_cols=N` | Fewest columns for landscape. | `6` |

```bash
ope export ./Notes -O tables.landscape=off
```

A template styles the landscape page with `@page landscape-page`, see [Header and footer](../templating/header-footer.md#landscape-pages).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/markdown/code/

# Code blocks

Fenced code blocks are highlighted by pandoc for the language after the fence. Inline code uses a monospace font.

Markdown:

````markdown
```python
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    """Return a friendly greeting."""
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
```

```bash
ope export ./Notes --title "Handbook"
```

```json
{ "theme": "base", "pages": 12 }
```
````

PDF:

![Highlighted Python, Bash and JSON code blocks](../img/features/code-blocks.png)

Code is shown as written. Wiki links, embeds, block IDs and `%%` comments inside code are not processed, as in Obsidian. A `mermaid` block is drawn as a diagram, see [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md). `dataview` blocks are run by the [Dataview](../plugins/dataview.md) plugin.

The colours of the highlighting come from pandoc's default style. A template can change them with the `span.kw`, `span.st`, `span.co` (and so on) classes inside `pre code`.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/markdown/quotes/

# Block quotes

Markdown:

````markdown
> Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability.
>
> > A quote can contain another quote.

> A quote can hold **formatting**,
> - lists
> - and more
````

PDF:

![Block quotes, nested and with a list](../img/features/blockquotes.png)

A quote that starts with `[!type]` is a callout, see [Callouts](../obsidian/callouts.md).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/markdown/footnotes/

# Footnotes

Footnotes work as in Obsidian: a reference `[^1]` with a definition `[^1]: text` anywhere in the note, or an inline note `^[text]`. Each note is shown at the bottom of the page where it is referenced. The numbers run through the whole document.

Markdown:

````markdown
Pandoc reads footnotes with a label[^label] or a number[^1].
Inline footnotes work too.^[This one is written in the text.]

[^label]: A footnote with a named label.
[^1]: A footnote with a number.
````

PDF:

![Footnote references in the text and the notes at the bottom of the page](../img/features/footnotes.png)

The dashed line in the picture marks where empty page space was cut out.

- The labels of each note (and of each embedded note) are kept apart, so `[^1]` on one page never shows the text of `[^1]` on another page.
- When two references use the same label, each gets its own copy of the note, with its own number.
- A note that holds a list, a table or another block besides paragraphs cannot be placed at the bottom of the page. It stays in the list of notes at the end of the document, with its number.

| Option | Effect | Default |
| ------ | ------ | ------- |
| `-O footnotes=page\|end` | `page` shows notes at the bottom of the page. `end` keeps one list of notes at the end of the document. | `page` |

The notes use CSS [paged media footnotes](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-gcpm-3/#footnotes) (`float: footnote`). To style them, see the [CSS reference](../templating/css-reference.md#footnotes).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/markdown/links-images/

# Links and images

## Links

Markdown:

````markdown
A Markdown link: [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md).

A bare URL: https://pandoc.org

An autolink: <https://github.com>

A link with a title: [WeasyPrint](https://weasyprint.org "PDF engine").
````

PDF:

![Markdown links and URLs](../img/features/links.png)

- A Markdown link and an autolink in angle brackets become links in the PDF.
- A bare URL stays plain text. Pandoc's reader does not turn it into a link, while Obsidian does. Wrap it in `<...>` to get a link.
- In print, links have the text colour. Links between pages of the export are [wiki links](../obsidian/wiki-links.md).

## Images

Markdown:

````markdown
An image followed by a single italic line:

![[chart.png|320]]
*The italic line becomes the caption.*

A caption written in the embed:

![[chart.png|Visits per month|240]]
````

PDF:

![Images with captions](../img/features/images.png)

- An image is at most as wide as the text and never split across pages.
- A single italic line right below an image becomes its caption.
- Image sizes and the full embed syntax are on the [Embeds](../obsidian/embeds.md) page.

!!! warning "Relative paths in Markdown images"
    A Markdown image with a relative path, such as `![Chart](../img/chart.png)`, is not looked up from the note's folder yet, so the image is missing in the PDF. Use an Obsidian embed (`![[chart.png]]`), which is looked up in the whole vault.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/markdown/html/

# Inline HTML

HTML in a note is passed to the PDF as it is, so tags such as `<kbd>`, `<sub>`, `<sup>`, `<u>` or a styled `<div>` work.

Markdown:

````markdown
Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd> to open the command palette.

Water is H<sub>2</sub>O and E = mc<sup>2</sup>.

<span style="color: #c53030">Red text</span> and <u>underlined text</u>.

A block of raw HTML with its own style.
````

PDF:

![Keyboard keys, sub and superscript, colored and boxed text](../img/features/inline-html.png)

HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) are removed. WeasyPrint draws the HTML, so scripts and interactive elements have no effect.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/markdown/math/

# Math

`$...$` is inline math, `$$...$$` display math. Formulas are rendered to SVG with [ziamath](https://github.com/cdelker/ziamath), so no TeX install is needed.

Markdown:

````markdown
Inline math such as $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$ sits in the text.

Display math is centered:

$$
\int_0^\infty e^{-x^2}\,dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}
$$

$$
\mathbf{A} = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}
$$
````

PDF:

![Inline and display math](../img/features/math.png)

Display math is centered. A formula takes the colour of the text around it, for example inside a callout. A formula that fails to render is shown as code, and the export prints a warning.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/

# Obsidian

The second layer of an export handles the syntax Obsidian adds to Markdown, without any community plugin. Each piece of syntax is a small step in [`core/steps/`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/tree/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/core/steps). All steps are listed in `CORE_STEPS` in `core/steps/__init__.py`.

## Features

| Feature | Page |
| ------- | ---- |
| Folders as sections, folder notes, table of contents, numbering | [Folder structure](structure.md) |
| `[[Page]]`, `[[Page\|alias]]`, `[[#Heading]]` | [Wiki links](wiki-links.md) |
| `![[image.png\|300]]`, `![[Note]]`, `![[Note#Heading]]`, `![[Note#^id]]` | [Embeds](embeds.md) |
| `^block-id` | [Block IDs](block-ids.md) |
| `> [!note] Title` | [Callouts](callouts.md) |
| `==highlight==`, `%% comment %%` | [Highlights and comments](highlights-comments.md) |
| `#tag` | [Tags](tags.md) |
| YAML frontmatter | [Properties](properties.md) |
| `- [ ] task` | [Tasks](tasks.md) |
| A newline is a line break | [Line breaks](line-breaks.md) |
| ` ```mermaid ` | [Mermaid](mermaid.md) |
| `[^1]`, `^[note]` | [Footnotes](../markdown/footnotes.md) |
| `![[Books.base]]`, ` ```base ` | [Bases](bases.md) |

## Order of the steps

The markdown steps run on every page in this order. The order matters: an embed inside an HTML comment is not expanded, because comments are removed first, and block IDs in embedded text are removed because embeds run before them.

| Priority | Step | Why here |
| -------- | ---- | -------- |
| 10 | `frontmatter` | Plugins read the parsed frontmatter. |
| 20 | `plugins` | Community plugins see Obsidian source syntax. |
| 30 | `html_comments` | Commented-out embeds are not expanded. |
| 35 | `bases` | Before embeds, so `![[x.base]]` is rendered as a view. |
| 38 | `pdf_embeds` | Before embeds, so `![[x.pdf#page=2]]` is not read as a note and heading. |
| 40 | `embeds` | Embedded content then passes all later steps. |
| 50 | `obsidian_comments` | After embeds, so embedded comments go too. |
| 60 | `block_ids` | After embeds, so embedded markers go too. |
| 65 | `footnotes` | After embeds, so each embedded note keeps its own labels. |
| 70 | `callouts` | |
| 80 | `heading_links` | Tags `[[#Heading]]` links with the page they are written on. |
| 90 | `wiki_links` | |
| 100 | `bracket_links` | After real wiki links are resolved. |
| 110 | `image_captions` | After `![[img]]` became an image. |
| 120 | `title_heading` | |
| 130 | `heading_levels` | Sees every heading of the page. |
| 135 | `plugin_code_blocks` | Warns about plugin code blocks nobody rendered. |
| 180 | `mermaid` | Runs once on the whole document. |

After pandoc, the HTML steps run: `base_css`, `empty_table_headers`, `column_widths`, `svg_images`, `heading_links`, `tasks`, `math`, `wide_tables`, `landscape_figures`, `footnotes` and `plugins`. [Contributing](../contributing.md) explains how to add a step.

## Content that is not rendered

Some content cannot be drawn in a PDF, or is not supported yet. It stays in the document in a simple form, and the export prints a line starting with `Warning:` that names the page:

- An embed of a file type other than notes, images and PDF files, such as `![[Board.canvas]]` or a video, becomes a link (or italic text when the file is not part of the export).
- A PDF embed that cannot be found or opened (for example an encrypted PDF) becomes a link the same way.
- An image that cannot be found becomes the italic text _[Image: name]_.
- A code block of a plugin ope does not render, such as ` ```tasks `, ` ```dataviewjs `, ` ```chart ` or an Admonition block ` ```ad-note `, stays a code block.
- DataviewJS and `TASK` queries become a short note in italics.

Check the warnings of an export to find such places:

```bash
ope export ./Vault 2>&1 | grep Warning:
```

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/structure/

# Folder structure

`ope export ROOT` walks the folder `ROOT`. Every subfolder becomes a section, and the note named like its folder is the text of that section:

```text
Handbook/
├── Handbook.md            ← root note, the first text of the document
├── images/                ← an attachments folder, its name does not matter
│   └── logo.png
├── Introduction/
│   └── Introduction.md    ← folder note of "Introduction"
├── Part A/
│   ├── Part A.md
│   ├── img/               ← scoped attachments, picked over images/ on ties
│   │   └── logo.png
│   ├── Chapter 1/
│   │   └── Chapter 1.md
│   └── Chapter 2/
│       └── Chapter 2.md
└── Part B/
    └── Part B.md
```

Markdown:

````markdown
The root note is the first page. Every folder below becomes a section.
````

PDF:

![Table of contents and numbered sections made from the folders](../img/features/structure.png)

## Rules

- Sections are sorted by folder name. The folder name is the section heading.
- Headings inside a note nest under the section heading, so a note's `##` sits one level below its folder.
- Folders without Markdown, such as attachment folders, are left out. `.git`, `.obsidian`, `.vscode` and every other dot folder are skipped.
- `--include` and `--exclude` pick top-level subfolders by name. `--no-toc` leaves out the table of contents.

## The root note

Three layouts are recognised:

1. `Handbook/Handbook.md` exists: it is the root note.
2. `Handbook/Handbook/Handbook.md` exists: the inner folder is the root, its siblings become sections.
3. Neither: the root has no text, the subfolders are the sections.

The mapping from folder to note is done by the [Folder Notes](../plugins/folder-notes.md) plugin, so a third-party plugin can change it (for example to `README.md` per folder).

## The vault

Links, embeds and images are looked up in the whole vault, not only in the exported folder. The vault is the folder that holds `.obsidian`, or else the root of the git repository. When several files share a name, the one closest to the linking page wins: `Part A/img/logo.png` beats `images/logo.png` for every page inside `Part A/`.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/wiki-links/

# Wiki links

A wiki link to a page of the export becomes a link to that page's section in the PDF.

Markdown:

````markdown
## Links

- Plain: [[Setup guide]]
- With alias: [[Setup guide|the setup guide]]
- To a heading on another page: [[Setup guide#Install]]
- With a folder path: [[wiki-links/Setup guide|setup guide by path]]
- To a heading on this page: [[#Links]]
- To a page outside the export: [[Missing page]]
````

PDF:

![Wiki links in the PDF](../img/features/wiki-links.png)

| Syntax | Result |
| ------ | ------ |
| `[[Page]]` | Link to the section of `Page`. |
| `[[Page\|alias]]` | Same link, showing the alias. |
| `[[#Heading]]`, `[[#Heading\|alias]]` | Link to the heading on the same page. When several pages share a heading name, the one on the linking page wins. |
| `[[Page#Heading]]`, `[[Page#Heading\|alias]]` | Link to that heading on `Page`. Without an alias the label is `Page > Heading`. When `Page` has no such heading, the link goes to the page. `[[Page#A#B]]` uses the last heading, `B`. |
| `[[Page#^id]]` | Link to the section of `Page`. |
| `[[Folder/Page]]`, `[[Page.md]]` | The last path part is the page name and a `.md` suffix is ignored. When several pages have that name, the one whose path ends with `Folder/Page` wins. |
| `[[Missing page]]` | A page outside the export shows as italic text. |
| `[[https://example.com\|text]]` | An external link. |

When two pages have the same name, the link goes to the one closest to the linking page. Each of them has its own anchor in the PDF (`page`, `page-1`, ...). Links inside code are left as written.

Standard Markdown links (`[text](https://...)`) are covered in [Links and images](../markdown/links-images.md).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/embeds/

# Embeds

## Images

`![[image.png]]` embeds an image from anywhere in the vault. A number sets the width in pixels, `WIDTHxHEIGHT` both. A caption can come first.

Markdown:

````markdown
Natural size, limited to the text width:

![[chart.png]]

Width in pixels:

![[chart.png|200]]

Width and height, with a caption first:

![[chart.png|Visits per month|300x100]]
````

PDF:

![Images at natural size, with a width, and with width, height and caption](../img/features/embed-images.png)

| Syntax | Result |
| ------ | ------ |
| `![[chart.png]]` | Natural size, at most the text width. |
| `![[chart.png\|300]]` | 300 px wide. |
| `![[chart.png\|300x100]]` | 300 by 100 px. |
| `![[chart.png\|Caption\|300]]` | A caption below the image, and a width. |
| `![[missing.png]]` | Shown as _[Image: missing.png]_. |

An image is at most as wide as the text and is never split across pages. PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP and SVG are supported.

## SVG

SVG files are inlined into the HTML, so lines and text stay sharp at any zoom and the text can be searched. draw.io exports get extra handling, see [draw.io](../plugins/drawio.md).

Markdown:

````markdown
SVG images are inlined, so they stay sharp:

![[shapes.svg]]

![[shapes.svg|180]]
````

PDF:

![An SVG file at natural size and at 180 pixels](../img/features/embed-svg.png)

## PDF

`![[file.pdf]]` draws the pages of a PDF file as images, one below the other, each with a thin border. The file name is the caption. A page is at most as wide as the text and at most 22 cm high.

Markdown:

````markdown
All pages of a PDF, 260 pixels wide:

![[slides.pdf|260]]

One page:

![[slides.pdf#page=2|260]]
````

PDF:

![A three-page PDF and one page of it, drawn as images](../img/features/embed-pdf.png)

| Syntax | Result |
| ------ | ------ |
| `![[file.pdf]]` | All pages, up to `pdf_embeds.max_pages`. |
| `![[file.pdf#page=3]]` | Only page 3. |
| `![[file.pdf#page=2-4]]` | Pages 2 to 4. |
| `![[file.pdf#height=400]]` | Every page 400 px high. |
| `![[file.pdf\|300]]` | Every page 300 px wide. `300x200` sets both. |

| Option | Default | Effect |
| ------ | ------- | ------ |
| `-O pdf_embeds.max_pages=N` | `10` | Most pages drawn per embed. When pages are left out, a line such as "… 4 more pages in file.pdf" follows the last page. |
| `-O pdf_embeds.dpi=N` | `150` | Resolution of the page images. Higher values are sharper and make a larger PDF. |
| `-O pdf_embeds=link` | `pages` | Keep PDF embeds as links, as before version 0.8. |

The pages are drawn with [pypdfium2](https://github.com/pypdfium2-team/pypdfium2), which is installed with ope and needs no system package. WeasyPrint cannot place a page of another PDF as vector content, so the pages are PNG images: text in them cannot be selected or searched. A PDF that cannot be found or opened, for example because it is encrypted, becomes a link and the export prints a warning. Embeds inside code stay as written.

Templates can style `figure.pdf-embed`, the page images `img.pdf-embed-page` and the note `p.pdf-embed-more`.

## Notes, headings and blocks

`![[Note]]` puts the content of another note in place, without its frontmatter. A heading or block reference embeds a part of it. The source note here is `_notes/Meeting notes.md`:

````markdown
---
type: meeting
date: 2026-03-02
status: done
---
# Meeting notes

## Decisions

- Ship version 2 in April.
- Keep the old export for one more release.

## Open points

The budget for the new server is still open. ^budget

| Item   | Cost |
| ------ | ---- |
| Server | 2400 |
| Backup | 300  |

^costs
````

Markdown:

````markdown
### Whole note

![[Meeting notes]]

### One heading

![[Meeting notes#Decisions]]

### One block

![[Meeting notes#^budget]]

### A table marked on the line below

![[Meeting notes#^costs]]
````

PDF:

![Embedded note, heading, block and table](../img/features/embed-notes.png)

| Syntax | Embeds |
| ------ | ------ |
| `![[Note]]` | The whole note. |
| `![[Note#Heading]]` | The heading and its content, up to the next heading of the same or a higher level. |
| `![[Note#A#B]]` | Heading `B` inside section `A`. |
| `![[Note#^id]]` | The block marked `^id`, see [Block IDs](block-ids.md). |
| `![[Note#^id-id]]` | A range, see [Block Link Plus](../plugins/block-link-plus.md). |

Embedded content is processed like the note it comes from:

- Plugin syntax (Dataview, Meta Bind, ...) uses the frontmatter and folder of the source note.
- Images and wiki links resolve from the source note's folder.
- Embeds inside embedded content are expanded too, up to 10 levels. An embed that would include itself again is skipped.
- Headings are shifted so the topmost one sits one level below the heading the embed is under. Without a heading above it, the page title counts. Nested headings keep their relative levels.
- An embed alone on its line (it may be indented, or in a quote or callout) becomes block content. An embed inside other text is inserted inline, with its lines joined.
- A note, heading or block that cannot be found shows as italic text, such as _Note#^id_, and the export prints a warning.

The target is looked up in the whole vault. `![[Note]]` picks the closest note of that name. A path such as `![[Folder/Note#^id]]` is matched against the end of each note's path.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/block-ids/

# Block IDs

A block ID (`^id`) at the end of a line marks that paragraph, list item or heading. A line with only `^id` marks the block right above it: a table, list, quote or callout. The IDs are used by [embeds](embeds.md#notes-headings-and-blocks) and removed from the output.

Markdown:

````markdown
Block IDs at the end of a line are removed from the output. ^first-point

- A list item with an ID ^item

> A quote with an ID on the line below

^quote
````

PDF:

![Text with the block IDs removed](../img/features/block-ids.png)

`^id-id` marks the end of a range for [Block Link Plus](../plugins/block-link-plus.md). Without that plugin it is a plain block ID.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/callouts/

# Callouts

## Types

Every Obsidian callout type works. Aliases share the style of their group: `[!summary]` looks like `[!abstract]`, `[!caution]` like `[!warning]`.

Markdown:

````markdown
> [!note]
> note

> [!abstract]
> abstract, summary, tldr

> [!info]
> info

> [!todo]
> todo

> [!tip]
> tip, hint, important

> [!success]
> success, check, done

> [!question]
> question, help, faq

> [!warning]
> warning, caution, attention

> [!failure]
> failure, fail, missing

> [!danger]
> danger, error

> [!bug]
> bug

> [!example]
> example

> [!quote]
> quote, cite
````

PDF:

![Every callout type with its colour](../img/features/callout-types.png)

| Group | Types |
| ----- | ----- |
| note | `note` |
| abstract | `abstract`, `summary`, `tldr` |
| info | `info` |
| todo | `todo` |
| tip | `tip`, `hint`, `important` |
| success | `success`, `check`, `done` |
| question | `question`, `help`, `faq` |
| warning | `warning`, `caution`, `attention` |
| failure | `failure`, `fail`, `missing` |
| danger | `danger`, `error` |
| bug | `bug` |
| example | `example` |
| quote | `quote`, `cite` |

Any other type, such as `[!information]`, looks like a note unless the template styles it.

## Titles, folding, nesting

Markdown:

````markdown
> [!tip] A custom title
> The title replaces the type name.

> [!faq]- Foldable callouts are always shown open
> The `+` and `-` markers are accepted.

> [!warning] Nested callouts
> Outer text.
>
> > [!info] Inner callout
> > Inner text.

> [!note] Lazy continuation
A line without `>` still belongs to the callout,
as in Obsidian.

| Status | Note |
| ------ | ---- |
| Done   | > [!success] Inline callout in a cell |
````

PDF:

![Custom title, foldable, nested, lazy and inline callouts](../img/features/callouts.png)

- The text after the type is the title. Without it, the type name is the title.
- The fold markers `[!faq]+` and `[!faq]-` are accepted. The callout is always shown open.
- Callouts nest with `> >`.
- Blank `>` lines stay inside the callout.
- A line right after a callout without `>` still belongs to it (lazy continuation), as in Obsidian.
- A single-line callout inside other text, for example in a table cell, becomes an inline callout.

## HTML and CSS

A callout becomes a `div` with the classes of its type and group, and a `data-callout` attribute:

```html
  <p><span class="callout-title"><strong>Title</strong></span></p>
  <p>Text</p>
```

An inline callout is a `span` with the same classes. To style a type, see the [CSS reference](../templating/css-reference.md#callouts).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/highlights-comments/

# Highlights and comments

## Highlights

`==text==` becomes `<mark>`.

Markdown:

````markdown
Mark the ==important words== in a sentence.

==A whole line can be highlighted.==
````

PDF:

![Highlighted words and a highlighted line](../img/features/highlights.png)

## Comments

`%% ... %%` comments, on one line or over several lines, and HTML comments are removed. Inside code they stay as written.

Markdown:

````markdown
This text is visible. %% This comment is not. %%

%%
A comment block over several lines
is removed as well.
%%

<!-- HTML comments are removed too. -->
The `%% text %%` inside code stays as written.
````

PDF:

![Only the visible text remains](../img/features/comments.png)

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/tags/

# Tags

Inline tags such as `#draft` or `#area/docs` stay in the text as plain text. Tags in the frontmatter are not shown. The [Dataview](../plugins/dataview.md) plugin uses both kinds for `FROM #tag` queries.

Markdown:

````markdown
Tags such as #draft and #status/review stay in the text as written.

Nested tags like #area/docs/pdf are kept as well.
````

PDF:

![Tags as plain text](../img/features/tags.png)

A tag at the start of a line is not a heading, because headings need a space after `#`.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/properties/

# Properties

The properties block (YAML frontmatter) at the top of a note is parsed and removed from the output. [Meta Bind](../plugins/meta-bind.md) and [Dataview](../plugins/dataview.md) read it.

Markdown:

````markdown
---
title: Release checklist
owner: Docs team
tags: [release, checklist]
---
The properties block at the top is parsed and removed. Plugins such as Meta Bind and Dataview read it.
````
