````markdown
The owner of this page is `VIEW[{owner}][text]`.
````

PDF:

![The frontmatter is gone, a Meta Bind view shows one value](../img/features/properties.png)

The title of the document comes from `--title` or the folder name, not from a `title` property.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/tasks/

# Tasks

`- [ ]` and `- [x]` become empty and checked boxes on the same line as the text, in a list without bullets.

Markdown:

````markdown
- [ ] Write the release notes
- [x] Update the version
- [ ] Review the PDF
    - [x] Check the table of contents
    - [ ] Check the footer
````

PDF:

![Open and done tasks, nested](../img/features/tasks.png)

The list is a `ul.task-list`. Status characters other than space and `x` (such as `[/]` or `[-]` from some themes) are not drawn as boxes.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/line-breaks/

# Line breaks

In Obsidian a single newline is a line break, unless "Strict line breaks" is on. ope reads that setting from `.obsidian/app.json` (`strictLineBreaks`).

Markdown:

````markdown
A single newline
is a line break,
as in Obsidian.

A blank line starts a new paragraph.
````

PDF:

![A newline is a line break](../img/features/line-breaks.png)

With strict line breaks, or with `-O line_breaks=soft`, lines of one paragraph are joined:

Markdown:

````markdown
A single newline
is a line break,
as in Obsidian.

A blank line starts a new paragraph.
````

PDF:

![Lines joined into one paragraph](../img/features/line-breaks-soft.png)

| Option | Effect |
| ------ | ------ |
| `-O line_breaks=hard` | A newline is always a line break. |
| `-O line_breaks=soft` | A newline is a space. A line break needs two trailing spaces or a backslash. |

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/mermaid/

# Mermaid

` ```mermaid ` blocks are drawn with [mermaid-cli](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli). ope uses `mmdc` if it is on the `PATH`, else `npx -y @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli@11.4.2` when Node.js is installed. Without either, the blocks stay code blocks and the export prints a warning. A block that fails to render also stays code.

Markdown:

````markdown
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Notes] --> B{Export}
    B -->|PDF| C[Readers]
    B -->|Redline| D[Reviewers]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    Author->>ope: export ./Notes
    ope->>Author: handbook.pdf
```
````

PDF:

![A flowchart and a sequence diagram](../img/features/mermaid.png)

The default output is SVG, so text stays sharp and can be searched. Mermaid normally puts labels in HTML `<foreignObject>` elements, which WeasyPrint does not draw, so for SVG output ope always sets `htmlLabels: false`. Use PNG for a diagram type that needs HTML labels.

## Options

| Option | Effect | Default |
| ------ | ------ | ------- |
| `-O mermaid=off` | Keep Mermaid blocks as code. | on |
| `-O mermaid.format=svg\|png` | Output format. | `svg` |
| `-O mermaid.scale=N` | Pixel density of PNG output. The image keeps its natural size. | `3` |
| `-O mermaid.config=PATH` | JSON [Mermaid config](https://mermaid.js.org/config/schema-docs/config.html) (`theme`, `themeVariables`, ...). | none |
| `-O mermaid.theme=NAME` | Shortcut for `theme`: `default`, `neutral`, `dark`, `forest`, `base`. | none |
| `-O mermaid.cli=COMMAND` | Command that runs mermaid-cli. | auto |
| `-O mermaid.puppeteer_config=PATH` | Puppeteer config passed as `-p`. | none |
| `-O mermaid.trim=on\|off` | Trim the empty space around diagrams. | `on` |
| `-O mermaid.max_height=LENGTH` | Largest height, such as `10cm`. Taller diagrams are scaled down. | none |
| `-O mermaid.landscape=on\|off` | Put wide diagrams on landscape pages. | `on` |
| `-O mermaid.landscape_ratio=R` | Width to height ratio from which a diagram that has to shrink goes to landscape. | `1.4` |
| `-O mermaid.landscape_min_font=PT` | Smallest text size a diagram may shrink to on a portrait page before it goes to landscape. | `7` |

A template can set a base config with the `mermaid` key in `template.yaml` or `Template.mermaid_config()`. `mermaid.config` is merged over it, then `mermaid.theme`.

```bash
ope export ./Notes -O mermaid.config=mermaid.json
```

```json
{ "theme": "base", "themeVariables": { "primaryColor": "#e8eef5", "pie1": "#2c5282" } }
```

## Diagram size

A diagram keeps its natural size and only shrinks when it is wider than the text. `mermaid.max_height` scales down taller ones. Other sizes belong in the template's CSS: every diagram has the classes `doc-image`, `mermaid` and `mermaid-<type>`, see [CSS reference](../templating/css-reference.md#mermaid-diagrams).

Mermaid leaves empty space around some diagram types. ope trims it to a margin of 8 px. PNG images are cropped. For SVG, mermaid-cli renders a second, transparent PNG to find the visible area, and ope shrinks the `viewBox`. That takes a few seconds, `-O mermaid.trim=off` skips it.

`%%` comment lines in a block are removed before rendering.

## Wide diagrams

A diagram wider than the text shrinks, and so does its text. When that makes it hard to read, the diagram goes to its own landscape page, like a [wide table](../markdown/tables.md#wide-tables).

Markdown:

````markdown
A wide diagram moves to its own landscape page:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Draft] --> B[Review] --> C[Approve] --> D[Export PDF] --> E[Sign] --> F[Publish] --> G[Archive] --> H[Retire]
```

Figure 1: The document life cycle

The text continues on a portrait page.
````

PDF:

![A wide flowchart on a landscape page, with its caption](../img/features/mermaid-landscape.png)

A diagram moves when it has to shrink to fit a portrait page and either its width is at least `mermaid.landscape_ratio` times its height, or its text would get smaller than `mermaid.landscape_min_font` points. It only moves when the landscape page shows it larger, so a tall diagram stays where it is. On the landscape page it is sized to fit the page height, with room for a caption.

A short paragraph right below the diagram that starts with a word and a number, such as `Figure 1: Overview`, is its caption and moves with it. The diagram gets the class `landscape`, its wrapper `wide-table-section landscape-figure`, so a template's landscape page for tables applies to diagrams too.

```bash
ope export ./Notes -O mermaid.landscape_ratio=2
ope export ./Notes -O mermaid.landscape=off
```

!!! note
    In the picture above the right edge of the last box is cut off. That comes from the trimming of empty space ([#69](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/issues/69)); `-O mermaid.trim=off` avoids it.

## Notes

- WeasyPrint clips text centered in a semi-transparent group. Gantt axis labels are drawn that way, so ope adds `.grid .tick { opacity: 1 }` to the `themeCSS` of SVG diagrams.
- Wrapped labels in timeline diagrams carry a line offset twice. ope removes the outer one, so the text stays in its box.
- Flowchart edge labels use `edgeLabelBackground`. With the `base` theme it can look purple. Set `themeVariables.edgeLabelBackground` to change it.
- When running as root (in a CI container), Chromium needs `--no-sandbox`. ope passes it in that case.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/bases/

# Bases

[Bases](https://help.obsidian.md/bases) is a core plugin of Obsidian. A base is a `.base` file, or a ` ```base ` code block, in YAML. It selects notes with filters and shows them in views. The export renders a view as it looks when the PDF is made. The notes here are the project notes shown on the [Dataview](../plugins/dataview.md) page.

Markdown:

````markdown
```base
filters:
  and:
    - file.hasTag("project")
views:
  - type: table
    name: Projects
    order:
      - file.name
      - owner
      - status
      - due
    sort:
      - property: due
        direction: ASC
  - type: list
    name: Open
    filters:
      and:
        - status != "done"
```
````

PDF:

![A table view of the project notes, sorted by due date](../img/features/bases.png)

## Views

- `![[Books.base]]` and ` ```base ` blocks show the first view. `![[Books.base#Reading list]]` shows the view with that name.
- `table` and `cards` views become a table, `list` views a bullet list. Other view types (`kanban`, `map`, views of community plugins) become a table, and the export prints a warning.
- Columns come from the view's `order` (only the file name when there is none), with the `displayName` from `properties` as header.
- The file name links to the note when the note is part of the export.
- `sort` (several properties, `ASC` or `DESC`, empty values last), `limit`, `groupBy` (a label line and a table per group), `groupOrder` and the view's `summaries` (a last row such as `Sum: 25.5`) work.
- The global `filters` and the view's `filters` both apply. `and`, `or` and `not` can be nested. `this` is the note that shows the base.

## Expressions

| Area | Supported |
| ---- | --------- |
| Literals | numbers, `"text"` and `'text'`, `true`, `false`, `null`, lists `[1, 2]`, objects, regular expressions `/a.c/gi` |
| Operators | `+ - * / %`, `== != > < >= <=`, `&& \|\| !`, `a ? b : c`, parentheses, `x.y`, `x["y"]`, `list[0]` |
| Properties | `price`, `note.price`, `note["my price"]`, `formula.name`, `file.*`, `this.*`. A name with a `-`, such as `due-date`, is a property when the note has one, otherwise a subtraction. |
| File fields | `name`, `basename`, `path`, `folder`, `ext`, `size`, `ctime`, `mtime`, `properties`, `tags`, `links`, `embeds`, `backlinks` |
| File functions | `hasTag()` (nested tags count), `inFolder()`, `hasLink()`, `hasProperty()`, `asLink()` |
| Global functions | `if()`, `date()`, `duration()`, `now()`, `today()`, `number()`, `list()`, `link()`, `file()`, `min()`, `max()`, `escapeHTML()`, `image()` |
| Any value | `isTruthy()`, `isType()`, `isEmpty()`, `toString()` |
| Text | `length`, `contains()`, `containsAll()`, `containsAny()`, `startsWith()`, `endsWith()`, `lower()`, `title()`, `trim()`, `replace()` (text or regular expression, `$1`), `repeat()`, `reverse()`, `slice()`, `split()` |
| Numbers | `abs()`, `ceil()`, `floor()`, `round()`, `toFixed()` |
| Lists | `length`, `contains()`, `containsAll()`, `containsAny()`, `filter()`, `map()`, `reduce()` (with `value`, `index`, `acc`), `flat()`, `join()`, `reverse()`, `slice()`, `sort()`, `unique()`, `mean()`, `sum()`, `min()`, `max()` |
| Dates | `year`, `month`, `day`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `millisecond`, `date()`, `format()` (Moment.js tokens), `time()`, `relative()`, `date + "1M"`, `date - "2h"`, `date - date` (milliseconds) |
| Links | `asFile()`, `linksTo()`, comparing links with files and `this` |
| Objects | `keys()`, `values()` |
| Regular expressions | `matches()` |
| Summaries | `Average`, `Min`, `Max`, `Sum`, `Range`, `Median`, `Stddev`, `Earliest`, `Latest`, `Checked`, `Unchecked`, `Empty`, `Filled`, `Unique`, and custom summaries with `values` |

Anything else, such as `html()`, `icon()`, `random()` or a function that does not exist, is not dropped silently: the export prints a warning that names the base and the expression. A filter that cannot be evaluated is ignored, so the view shows more notes rather than fewer. A column that cannot be evaluated stays empty.

Property types come from the YAML: a date written as `2024-05-01` is a date. The types set in Obsidian (`.obsidian/types.json`) are not read. Dates are shown as `YYYY-MM-DD`, checkboxes as ☑ and ☐.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/

# Plugins

The third layer handles syntax and files from community Obsidian plugins and other tools. Each plugin support module lives in its own package under [`plugins/`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/tree/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins), is found through an entry point and runs inside the `plugins` step of the [core steps](../obsidian/index.md#order-of-the-steps).

## Built-in plugins

| Name | Obsidian plugin | What it does | Priority |
| ---- | --------------- | ------------ | -------- |
| `folder_notes` | [Folder Notes](https://github.com/LostPaul/obsidian-folder-notes) | `Folder/Folder.md` is the text of its folder. [More](folder-notes.md) | 5 |
| `dataview` | [Dataview](https://github.com/blacksmithgu/obsidian-dataview) | Renders `TABLE` and `LIST` queries as static tables and lists. [More](dataview.md) | 10 |
| `excalidraw` | [Excalidraw](https://github.com/zsviczian/obsidian-excalidraw-plugin) | Turns drawing embeds into images. [More](excalidraw.md) | 15 |
| `meta_bind` | [Meta Bind](https://github.com/mProjectsCode/obsidian-meta-bind-plugin) | Fills `VIEW[...]` fields from the frontmatter, removes inputs and buttons. [More](meta-bind.md) | 20 |
| `block_link_plus` | [Block Link Plus](https://github.com/Jasper-1024/block-link-plus) | Resolves `![[Note#^id-id]]` range embeds. [More](block-link-plus.md) | 30 |
| `drawio` | [draw.io](https://www.drawio.com/) SVG exports | Turns HTML labels into SVG text. [More](drawio.md) | 40 |
| `citations` | [Citations](https://github.com/hans/obsidian-citation-plugin), Zotero integrations | Renders `[@key]` citations and a reference list with pandoc citeproc. [More](citations.md) | 50 |

```bash
ope list-plugins
```

shows the same list at runtime, including third-party plugins you installed.

## Turn a plugin off

```bash
ope export ./Vault --disable-plugin dataview --disable-plugin meta_bind
```

## Pass options

```bash
ope export ./Vault -O dataview.limit=200
```

`-O key=value` reaches every plugin hook as `context.options`. Plugin options use the name of the plugin as prefix: `<plugin>.<key>`.

## Third-party plugins

Any Python package can register a plugin under the `obsidian_pdf_exporter.obsidian_plugins` entry point. After `pip install` (or `uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter --with <package>`) it is used without any change to ope. See [Write a plugin](write-a-plugin.md).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/folder-notes/

# Folder Notes

The [Folder Notes](https://github.com/LostPaul/obsidian-folder-notes) plugin stores the note of a folder inside it, with the folder's name: `Chapter A/Chapter A.md`. The `folder_notes` plugin maps that note onto its folder while the page tree is built, so the note becomes the text of the folder's section.

The result is shown on [Folder structure](../obsidian/structure.md). Without this plugin (`--disable-plugin folder_notes`) the folders have no text.

A third-party plugin can change the convention with the `find_folder_note` hook, for example to use `Folder/README.md` or the note with `folder-note: true` in its frontmatter. See [Write a plugin](write-a-plugin.md#hooks).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/dataview/

# Dataview

The `dataview` plugin runs [Dataview](https://github.com/blacksmithgu/obsidian-dataview) queries at export time and writes the result as a Markdown table or list. The project notes queried here look like this:

````markdown
---
tags: [project]
status: active
owner: Ana
due: 2026-05-01
---
Notes about Website relaunch.
````

Markdown:

````markdown
```dataview
TABLE status, owner, due
FROM #project
SORT due ASC
```

```dataview
LIST
FROM "_notes/Projects"
WHERE status != "done"
```
````

PDF:

![A table and a list built from the query results](../img/features/dataview.png)

## Supported queries

- `TABLE` (with `WITHOUT ID`) and `LIST`.
- `FROM #tag` and `FROM "folder"`, combined with `AND` and `OR`, negated with `-`.
- `WHERE` with `field = "x"`, `field != "x"`, `NOT`, `AND`, `OR` and bare fields.
- `SORT field ASC|DESC` and `LIMIT n`.

`TASK`, `CALENDAR` and `dataviewjs` blocks are replaced with a placeholder text. Other queries are left as they are.

The query runs over the whole vault (the folder with `.obsidian`, or the git repository). Without a vault root the blocks stay as they are.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/excalidraw/

# Excalidraw

The `excalidraw` plugin turns embeds of [Excalidraw](https://github.com/zsviczian/obsidian-excalidraw-plugin) drawings into images.

Markdown:

````markdown
An Excalidraw drawing from the vault:

![[Drawing.excalidraw|420]]
````

PDF:

![An Excalidraw drawing with shapes, fills, an arrow, free drawing, text and an image](../img/features/excalidraw.png)

## Embeds

| Syntax | Finds |
| ------ | ----- |
| `![[Drawing.excalidraw]]`, `![[Drawing.excalidraw.md]]` | The drawing note `Drawing.excalidraw.md`. |
| `![[Drawing]]` | Any note with `excalidraw-plugin` in its frontmatter. |
| `![[Sketch.excalidraw]]` | A plain `.excalidraw` JSON file, as saved by excalidraw.com. |
| `![[Drawing.excalidraw\|400]]` | A width, as for images. |

## Auto-export files first

When the plugin's "Auto-export SVG" or "Auto-export PNG" setting wrote `Drawing.excalidraw.svg` (or `.light.svg`, `.png`, `.light.png`) next to the drawing, that file is used as it is. It looks exactly like the drawing in Obsidian. `-O excalidraw.auto_export=off` turns this off.

## Drawn from the scene

Otherwise ope reads the scene from the `## Drawing` section of the note (a ` ```json ` block, or ` ```compressed-json ` in LZ-String base64) and draws it as SVG. Excalidraw's hand-drawn look comes from rough.js in the browser. ope draws the same shapes with clean strokes, so the export needs neither Node.js nor a browser.

| Drawn | Not drawn (with a warning) |
| ----- | -------------------------- |
| Rectangles (also rounded), diamonds, ellipses | Embedded web pages, shown as an outlined box with their link |
| Solid fills; hachure, cross-hatch and zigzag fills as straight hatching | LaTeX equations |
| Lines, curves, elbow arrows and all arrowheads | Embedded notes, PDFs and drawings inside a drawing |
| Free drawing, as a line of even width | Image cropping (the whole image is drawn) |
| Text, also inside shapes and on arrows | Element links and `#^group=`, `#^area=`, `#^frame=` parts of an embed (the whole drawing is shown) |
| Images from the vault or a data URL, mirrored images | |
| Stroke colour, width, dashed and dotted strokes, opacity, rotation | |

Frames are not drawn, as in an Excalidraw export. Text uses the Excalidraw fonts when they are installed and falls back to a sans-serif or monospace font. The frontmatter keys `excalidraw-export-transparent` and `excalidraw-export-padding` are honoured. Dark drawings are drawn with their light colours.

For an exact copy of the hand-drawn look, turn on auto-export in the Excalidraw plugin.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/meta-bind/

# Meta Bind

The `meta_bind` plugin fills [Meta Bind](https://github.com/mProjectsCode/obsidian-meta-bind-plugin) `VIEW` fields with the values of the page's frontmatter. `INPUT` and `BUTTON` fields have no PDF form and are removed.

Markdown:

````markdown
---
product: Example App
version: 2.4.0
released: 2026-04-15
platforms: |
  - Linux
  - macOS
---
Release notes for `VIEW[{product}][text]` version `VIEW[{version}][text]`.

Released on `VIEW[{released}][date(D MMMM YYYY)]` (`VIEW[{released}][date(DD.MM.YYYY)]`).

| Field     | Value                                     |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Product   | `VIEW[{product} + " " + {version}][text]` |
| Platforms | `VIEW[{platforms}][text]`                 |

Input fields such as `INPUT[text:version]` are removed.
````

PDF:

![View fields filled with the frontmatter values](../img/features/meta-bind.png)

- `{key}` is the value of a frontmatter field. `+` joins values and quoted text.
- `[date(D MMMM YYYY)]` and `[datetime(DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm)]` format an ISO date or date and time with moment.js tokens: `D`, `DD`, `M`, `MM`, `MMM`, `MMMM`, `YY`, `YYYY`, `H`, `HH`, `mm` and `ss`. Month names are English. Other text in the format is kept. A value that is not a date is shown as written.
- A multi-line value shown inside text, such as in a table cell, stays in its cell: list items become an HTML list, other lines are joined with line breaks. A field alone on its line keeps the lines as they are.
- Fields inside code blocks are left as written.
- In an embedded note, the fields use the embedded note's frontmatter.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/block-link-plus/

# Block Link Plus

[Block Link Plus](https://github.com/Jasper-1024/block-link-plus) extends block references to ranges: `^id` marks the first block, `^id-id` the last one. `![[Note#^id-id]]` embeds everything from the first to the last block. The source note:

````markdown
# Procedure

Before the range.

1. Check out the repository. ^steps
2. Run the export.
3. Review the PDF. ^steps-steps

After the range.
````

Markdown:

````markdown
The steps from the procedure:

![[Procedure#^steps-steps]]
````

PDF:

![Only the steps of the range are embedded](../img/features/block-link-plus.png)

The end marker can also sit on its own line below a block, for example after a list or table. When the first line of a range is empty, Block Link Plus writes a `%% %% ^id` placeholder, which also works. Without this plugin, `^id-id` is looked up as a plain block ID.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/drawio/

# draw.io

draw.io stores labels as HTML in `<foreignObject>`, which WeasyPrint does not draw. Next to each label it writes a short fallback text and a "Text is not SVG - cannot display" note. The `drawio` plugin replaces each label with SVG text, one `<tspan>` per line, and removes the note.

Markdown:

````markdown
A draw.io diagram exported as SVG with HTML labels:

![[flow.drawio.svg]]
````

PDF:

![A draw.io diagram with readable labels](../img/features/drawio.png)

This is a best effort:

- Mixed formatting inside one label (a bold word, a second colour) is flattened to the main style of the label.
- Wrapped labels are wrapped again with an estimated character width, so line breaks can differ a little from draw.io.
- For full fidelity, export from draw.io with "Convert labels to SVG" turned on, or as PNG.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/citations/

# Citations

The `citations` plugin renders [pandoc citations](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#citation-syntax) with `pandoc --citeproc`, as the [Citations](https://github.com/hans/obsidian-citation-plugin) plugin and the Zotero integration plugins write them. The bibliography of this example is `examples/_attachments/references.bib`.

Markdown:

````markdown
---
bibliography: ../_attachments/references.bib
---
Typesetting is covered in depth by [@knuth1984, p. 12].
Several sources at once: [see @knuth1984; @lamport1995].
@lamport1995 shows how to structure a proof.

## References
````

PDF:

![Citations in the text and the reference list](../img/features/citations.png)

| Written | Rendered (default Chicago author-date style) |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `[@doe2020]` | (Doe 2020) |
| `[@doe2020, p. 12]` | (Doe 2020, 12) |
| `[see @doe2020; @roe2021]` | (see Doe 2020; Roe 2021) |
| `[-@doe2020]` | (2020) |
| `@doe2020 shows` | Doe (2020) shows |

## Bibliography

The bibliography is the first one found of:

1. `-O citations.bibliography=refs.bib` (several files separated by `,`). Relative paths start at the current folder or the exported folder.
2. The export path of the Citations plugin: `citationExportPath` in `.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-citation-plugin/data.json`, relative to the vault.
3. `bibliography:` in the frontmatter of the exported notes (a path or a list), relative to the note.

BibLaTeX and BibTeX (`.bib`, `.bibtex`), CSL JSON (`.json`) and CSL YAML (`.yaml`) work.

## Options

| Option | Effect |
| ------ | ------ |
| `-O citations.bibliography=PATH` | Bibliography files, separated by `,`. |
| `-O citations.csl=PATH` | A [CSL style](https://www.zotero.org/styles). `csl:` in the frontmatter does the same. |
| `-O citations.title=TEXT` | Heading of the reference list when ope adds one. |
| `-O citations=off` | Leave citations as written. |

## Where the reference list goes

The list goes into a `::: {#refs}` block when the document has one, otherwise below the last heading named `References`, `Bibliography`, `Works cited`, `Literature` or `Sources`. Without either, a `References` heading and the list are added at the end. Citations link to their entry.

`@word` outside brackets becomes a citation only when `word` is a key of the bibliography, so `@mentions` and e-mail addresses stay text. A link to a literature note such as `[[@doe2020]]` becomes the in-text citation `@doe2020` when the note is not part of the export.

Without a bibliography, citations stay as written and the export prints one warning. A citation whose key is not in the bibliography also prints a warning, and pandoc shows it as `(doe2020?)`.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/write-a-plugin/

# Write a plugin

A plugin support module is a subclass of [`ObsidianPlugin`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/base.py) that overrides the hooks it needs. It can live in this repository or in a package of its own. Support for core Obsidian syntax is a step, not a plugin, see [Contributing](../contributing.md).

## Example: strip Tasks metadata

The [Tasks](https://github.com/obsidian-tasks-group/obsidian-tasks) plugin adds emoji metadata such as `📅 2026-05-10` to task lines. This plugin removes it:

```python title="my_ope_plugins/tasks.py"
from __future__ import annotations

import re

from obsidian_pdf_exporter.plugins.base import ObsidianPlugin
from obsidian_pdf_exporter.plugins.base import PluginContext

_METADATA = re.compile(r"\s+[⏫🔼🔽📅⏳🛫✅❌🔁][^\n]*")

class TasksPlugin(ObsidianPlugin):
    """Remove the emoji metadata of the Tasks plugin."""

    name = "tasks"
    description = "Remove Tasks plugin metadata from task lines"
    priority = 60  # after the built-in plugins (5 to 50)

    def process_markdown(self, content: str, context: PluginContext) -> str:
        return _METADATA.sub("", content)
```

Register it under the entry point group in the package's `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project.entry-points."obsidian_pdf_exporter.obsidian_plugins"]
tasks = "my_ope_plugins.tasks:TasksPlugin"
```

Install it next to ope and check that it is found:

```bash
uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter --with ./my-ope-plugins
ope list-plugins
```

## Hooks

All hooks have no-op defaults.

| Hook | Runs | Used by |
| ---- | ---- | ------- |
| `find_folder_note(folder)` | While the page tree is built. Returns the note of a folder or `None`. The first plugin with a result wins. | `folder_notes` |
| `process_markdown(content, context)` | On each page and on embedded notes, after the frontmatter is parsed and before embeds, callouts and wiki links. | `dataview`, `meta_bind`, `excalidraw` |
| `process_document(markdown, context)` | On the assembled Markdown of the whole document, after `process_markdown` ran on every page. | `citations` |
| `reader_extensions(context)`, `pandoc_args(context)` | When the pandoc call is built, after `process_document`. Return extra reader extensions and arguments, such as `--citeproc`. | `citations` |
| `extract_block(body, block_id)` | For `![[Note#^id]]`. Returns the selected text or `None`, before core looks for `^id`. | `block_link_plus` |
| `process_svg(svg, context)` | On each SVG image while it is inlined. | `drawio` |
| `process_html(html, context)` | On the HTML of the whole document, after the core HTML steps and before the template. | `meta_bind` |

`PluginContext` (markdown hooks) has `vault_root`, `page_folder`, `frontmatter`, `options` and `vault_index`. `vault_root` is `None` when the export runs outside a vault, so a plugin that needs vault-wide data should do nothing then.

`DocumentContext` (SVG and HTML hooks) has `build_dir`, `options`, `root`, `export` (title, version, date), `template`, `plugins`, `redline` and `log`.

## Priority

`priority` is an integer, lower runs earlier. The built-ins use 5 (`folder_notes`), 10 (`dataview`), 15 (`excalidraw`), 20 (`meta_bind`), 30 (`block_link_plus`), 40 (`drawio`) and 50 (`citations`). Pick a value after the plugins whose output you need: a plugin that reads tables made by Dataview runs after 10.

## Guarantees

- The frontmatter is parsed and removed before `process_markdown` runs.
- Plugins run before embeds, callouts, wiki links and image captions, so their output passes the rest of the pipeline like written Markdown.
- Plugins also run on embedded notes, with the context of the embedded note.
- Keep code as written. Wrap a rewrite in `outside_code` from `obsidian_pdf_exporter.core.code`, as Obsidian does not process code.

## In this repository

A plugin for a broadly used Obsidian plugin can go into `obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/<name>/` with an `__init__.py` that exports the class and a thin `plugin.py`. Put larger parsing code in a module next to it, as Dataview does with `engine.py`. Add the entry point to the project's `pyproject.toml`, unit tests in `tests/unit/`, a page in these docs and an example in `examples/`.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templating/

# Templates and styling

A template decides how the PDF looks: fonts, colours, page size and margins, the running header and footer, and the style of every element. It does not change what is in the document. That is the job of the [steps](../obsidian/index.md) and [plugins](../plugins/index.md).

The PDF is laid out by [WeasyPrint](https://weasyprint.org/), which supports [CSS Paged Media](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-page-3/): `@page` rules, margin boxes, running elements, named pages and page counters. Templates are written in that CSS.

## Built-in templates

| Name | Look |
| ---- | ---- |
| `default` | A4 portrait. Document title at the top left, date at the bottom left, version and page counter at the bottom right. |
| `redline` | Same as `default`, plus the styles for [tracked changes](../redline.md). Used by `ope redline`. |

![A page with the default template](../img/templates/default.png)
![The same page with the letterhead recipe](../img/templates/letterhead.png)

## Three ways to make a template

| Way | Good for | Page |
| --- | -------- | ---- |
| One CSS file: `-T ./brand.css` | Changing styles only. | [Template folders](folders.md#a-single-css-file) |
| A folder with CSS, `template.yaml`, header HTML and page CSS: `-T ./my-template/` | A logo, a letterhead, a new footer. No Python. | [Template folders](folders.md) |
| A Python class registered as entry point | Header and footer text from the title, version or `-O` options, changes to Markdown or HTML. | [Python templates](python.md) |

Start with the [recipes](recipes.md): each one is a complete template with a picture of the result.

## How `--template` is resolved

```bash
ope export ./Vault --template default        # a name
ope export ./Vault --template ./brand.css    # a CSS file
ope export ./Vault --template ./my-template  # a folder
ope list-templates                           # every name and where it comes from
```

1. A value that is an existing path is loaded as a CSS file or template folder.
2. Any other value is a name, looked up in this order (a later source wins on equal names):
    1. built-in templates,
    2. templates of installed packages (entry point group `obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates`),
    3. folders in the user templates folder,
    4. templates registered at runtime with `register_template()`.

The user templates folder is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templates` (default `~/.config/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templates`). `OBSIDIAN_PDF_EXPORTER_TEMPLATES_DIR` points it somewhere else. Each subfolder is a template folder, named after the folder or the `name` in its `template.yaml`.

An unknown name ends the export with exit code 2.

## What a template does in an export

```text
notes → steps and plugins → template.process_markdown → pandoc → HTML steps
      → template.process_html → header/footer HTML and page CSS added → WeasyPrint → PDF
```

The template CSS is linked from the HTML. Its rules come after the base CSS of ope, so a template can restyle everything ope adds. The [CSS reference](css-reference.md) lists the elements and classes to style. [Debugging](debugging.md) shows how to look at the HTML WeasyPrint gets.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templating/folders/

# Template folders

## A single CSS file

```bash
ope export ./Vault --template ./brand.css
```

The file is the whole CSS of the PDF. Its name without `.css` is the template name. A single file has no running header or footer HTML, but it can use `@page` margin boxes with text and counters, see [Header and footer](header-footer.md).

The CSS replaces the `default` CSS completely. To change only a few things, start from a copy of [`default.css`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/templates/builtin/default/default.css) and add your rules at the end:

```bash
curl -o brand.css https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/templates/builtin/default/default.css
```

## A folder

```text
my-template/
├── template.yaml   # optional
├── main.css        # the CSS of the PDF
├── header.html     # optional: running header and footer elements
├── page.css        # optional: @page rules for the header and footer
├── logo.svg        # optional: assets, copied next to the CSS
└── fonts/
    └── Inter.woff2 # optional: list sub-folder assets in template.yaml
```

```bash
ope export ./Vault --template ./my-template/
```

### template.yaml

Every key is optional.

```yaml
name: legal-pack                 # default: the folder name
description: Cover sheet style   # shown by `ope list-templates`
css: main.css                    # default: template.css, or the only *.css file
running_html: header.html        # HTML put right after <body>
page_css: page.css               # CSS put into <head> after the template CSS
assets: [logo.svg, fonts/Inter.woff2]  # default: every other file in the folder
mermaid:                         # base Mermaid config for diagrams
  theme: base
  themeVariables:
    primaryColor: "#e8eef5"
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | ------- | ------- |
| `name` | folder name | Name in `list-templates` and for `--template` when the folder is in the user templates folder. |
| `description` | empty | One line for `list-templates`. |
| `css` | `template.css` or the only `*.css` file | The main CSS. With more than one CSS file and no `css` key, loading fails. |
| `running_html` | none | HTML for the running header and footer. It is put right after `<body>`, so its elements can be moved into margin boxes. |
| `page_css` | none | CSS for the page: `@page` rules and running elements. |
| `assets` | every file in the folder that is not CSS, YAML, HTML or Markdown, plus a sibling `assets/` folder | Files copied into the build folder next to the CSS. |
| `mermaid` | none | Base [Mermaid config](../obsidian/mermaid.md#options). `-O mermaid.config` and `-O mermaid.theme` are merged over it. |

Without `running_html` and `page_css` the template has no header or footer. The `default` header and footer come from Python and are not part of a folder template. A folder template that should have them writes them in `page.css`, as in the [recipes](recipes.md).

### Assets: logos and fonts

Assets are copied into the build folder next to the CSS, so `main.css` refers to them by relative path:

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Inter";
  src: url("fonts/Inter.woff2");
}
:root { --font-sans: "Inter", Arial, sans-serif; }
```

In `header.html` and `page.css`, every `src="..."` and `url(...)` that names an asset is replaced by a base64 data URI when the template is loaded. WeasyPrint does not resolve relative URLs from elements inside page margin boxes, so this is what makes a logo in the header work:

```html
<img class="brand-logo" src="logo.svg" alt="Logo">
```

External URLs (`https://...`) and names that are not assets are left as they are.

Fonts can also come from the system: any font installed for Fontconfig can be named in `font-family`.

### Sharing assets between templates

A folder named `assets/` next to the template folders is found too. Its files are referenced as `../assets/<name>`:

```text
templates/
├── assets/
│   └── logo.svg
├── letterhead/
│   └── header.html   # <img src="../assets/logo.svg">
└── compact/
```

The same path works in an explicit list: `assets: ['../assets/logo.svg']`.

## A named template for every vault

Put the folder into the user templates folder to use it by name from anywhere:

```text
~/.config/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templates/
└── legal-pack/
    ├── template.yaml
    └── main.css
```

```bash
ope list-templates
ope export ./Vault --template legal-pack
```

To share a template with a team, keep the folder in a repository and pass its path, or publish it as a [Python package](python.md#publish-as-a-package).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templating/header-footer/

# Header and footer

Headers and footers are drawn in the page margins with [CSS Paged Media](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-page-3/). A template puts content there in three ways:

| Way | Content | Where it is defined |
| --- | ------- | ------------------- |
| Text and counters in a margin box | Fixed text, page numbers | `page.css`, or any CSS of the template |
| Named strings (`string-set`) | Text copied from the document, such as the title | `page.css` |
| Running elements (`position: running()`) | Any HTML: a logo, several lines, styled spans | `header.html` plus `page.css` |

## Margin boxes

Every page has 16 margin boxes around the page area. The ones used most:

```text
┌─────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐
│ @top-left   │ @top-center  │ @top-right   │
├─────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┤
│                                           │
│                 page area                 │
│                                           │
├─────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┤
│ @bottom-left│@bottom-center│ @bottom-right│
└─────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┘
```

A box shows its `content`. Text, `counter(page)`, `counter(pages)`, `string(...)` and `element(...)` can be combined:

```css
@page {
  @bottom-right {
    content: "Page " counter(page) " of " counter(pages);
    font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
    font-size: 7pt;
    color: #606872;
  }
}
```

A margin box does not inherit the font of `body`. Set `font-family` and `font-size` in each box. `\A` in a string is a line break when the box has `white-space: pre`.

The margins of `@page` are the room for the boxes. A header that is 20pt tall in a 25mm top margin leaves about 5mm between the header and the text. Widen the margin or shrink the header.

## Named strings: text from the document

`string-set` copies the text of an element into a named string. A margin box shows it with `string()`. The title block that ope writes at the start of every document holds the title, subtitle and the version line:

```html
<header id="title-block-header">
  <h1 class="title">Team handbook</h1>
  <p class="subtitle">How we work</p>
  <p class="author">1.2.0 | 2026-04-01</p>
</header>
```

So a template folder, which has no Python, can still show them:

```css
header#title-block-header .title  { string-set: doc-title content(); }
header#title-block-header .author { string-set: doc-meta content(); }

@page {
  @top-left    { content: string(doc-title); }
  @bottom-left { content: string(doc-title) " · " string(doc-meta); }
}
```

The `author` line holds the version label and the date: `--version` or the short commit hash, then `--date`.

## Running elements: HTML in the margin

An element with `position: running(name)` is taken out of the page flow and can be placed in a margin box with `element(name)`. In a template folder, the elements are written in `header.html` (the `running_html` of `template.yaml`), which ope puts right after `<body>`:

```html title="header.html"
<img class="logo" src="logo.svg" alt="Logo">
```

```css title="page.css"
.logo    { position: running(logo); width: 40mm; }
.address { position: running(address); font-size: 7pt; }

@page {
  @top-right { content: element(logo); vertical-align: bottom; }
}
@page :first {
  @top-left { content: element(address); vertical-align: bottom; }
}
```

The `default` template uses a running element for its header too: `div.pdf-running-header` with `span.pdf-header-title` and `span.pdf-header-subtitle`, placed in `@top-left`.

A running element must come before the first page it appears on. Elements in `header.html` are at the very start of the document, so they show from page 1.

Images and fonts in `header.html` and `page.css` are turned into data URIs when the template is loaded, see [assets](folders.md#assets-logos-and-fonts).

## First page and other page selectors

```css
@page :first {
  margin-top: 40mm;                       /* room for a letterhead */
  @top-left { content: element(address); }
}
@page :first { @top-left { content: none; } }  /* no header on page 1 */
@page :left  { @bottom-left  { content: counter(page); } }
@page :right { @bottom-right { content: counter(page); } }
@page :blank { @top-left { content: none; } }
```

`:left` and `:right` are useful for printed, double-sided documents.

## Landscape pages

[Wide tables](../markdown/tables.md#wide-tables) and [wide diagrams](../obsidian/mermaid.md#wide-diagrams) are placed on a named page, `landscape-page`. A template that changes the page margins or the header should set them for that page too, or the landscape pages keep the old margins:

```css
@page landscape-page {
  size: A4 landscape;
  margin: 20mm 20mm 18mm 20mm;
  @top-left { content: string(doc-title); }
}
```

ope wraps each wide table and diagram in `.wide-table-section`. The template's CSS sends that wrapper to the named page. `default.css` does it like this, and a template written from scratch needs the same rules:

```css
@page landscape-page { size: A4 landscape; margin: 25mm 20mm 22mm 20mm; }
.wide-table-section { page: landscape-page; break-before: page; break-after: page; }
```

Margin boxes of the plain `@page` rule also apply to the named page unless the named page sets them.

## Escaping

- HTML in `header.html` or `running_html` must be valid: write `&amp;`, `&lt;` and `&quot;`.
- Text in a CSS string needs CSS escaping: `\` becomes `\\`, `"` becomes `\"` and a newline `\A `. Python templates build these strings from user data, so escape them there (see [Python templates](python.md)).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templating/css-reference/

# CSS reference

The HTML WeasyPrint lays out is pandoc's HTML plus the markup the steps and plugins add. This page lists what a template can style. To see the HTML of a real export, use [`--debug`](debugging.md).

## Order of the CSS

1. The base CSS of ope (`<style id="obsidian-pdf-exporter-base">`), at the start of `<head>`. It holds working defaults for the markup ope adds, so a template does not need rules for it.
2. The template CSS (`get_css()` or the folder's main CSS).
3. The template's `page_css`, if any.

A later rule wins, so a template can restyle everything from the base CSS.

## Colour and font variables of `default`

`default.css` keeps its colours and fonts in custom properties on `:root`. A template that starts from a copy of it can change the look by changing these:

| Variable | Default | Used for |
| -------- | ------- | -------- |
| `--color-accent` | `#2c5282` | Accent, link colour on screen |
| `--color-grey` | `#606872` | Secondary text, header row of tables, section numbers |
| `--color-light-grey` | `#f5f5f5` | Even table rows, code background |
| `--color-mid-grey` | `#e0e2e4` | Borders, rules |
| `--color-dark` | `#1a1a1a` | Body text |
| `--color-link` | `var(--color-accent)` | Links |
| `--font-sans` | `'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif` | Body text, header and footer |
| `--font-mono` | `'Courier New', monospace` | Code |
| `--page-margin` | `20mm` | Defined for templates to reuse. The `@page` rule of `default` sets its margins directly. |

The `redline` template adds `--color-ins-bg`, `--color-ins-text`, `--color-del-bg` and `--color-del-text`.

## Document structure

| Selector | What it is |
| -------- | ---------- |
| `html`, `body` | Base font size and font. `default` uses `html { font-size: 12pt }`. |
| `header#title-block-header` | Title block at the start: `h1.title`, `p.subtitle`, `p.author` (version label and date). |
| `nav#TOC` | Table of contents: nested `ul`, links, `span.toc-section-number`. |
| `h1` ... `h6` | Headings. The top-level sections are `h1`. Each has `data-number` and an `id`. |
| `.header-section-number` | The number in front of a heading. |
| `div.pdf-running-header`, `.pdf-header-title`, `.pdf-header-subtitle` | Running header of the `default` and `redline` templates. |

## Text

| Selector | What it is |
| -------- | ---------- |
| `p`, `strong`, `em`, `del` | Paragraphs and emphasis. In a redline, `del` is also removed text. |
| `mark` | [Highlights](../obsidian/highlights-comments.md). |
| `a` | Links. `a.heading-link` is a `[[#Heading]]` link. `default` prints links in the text colour. |
| `blockquote` | Block quotes. Callouts are not block quotes. |
| `hr` | Horizontal rules. |
| `code`, `pre`, `pre code` | Inline code and code blocks. Highlighting uses pandoc's classes inside `pre code`: `span.kw` (keyword), `span.st` (string), `span.co` (comment), `span.dv` (number), `span.fu` (function) and more. |
| `ul`, `ol`, `li` | Lists. |
| `ul.task-list`, `span.task-checkbox`, `span.task-checkbox.checked` | [Tasks](../obsidian/tasks.md). The boxes are the glyphs ☐ and ☑. |
| `dl`, `dt`, `dd` | Definition lists (pandoc syntax). |

## Tables

| Selector | What it is |
| -------- | ---------- |
| `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td` | Tables. `colgroup > col` holds the column widths ope computed. |
| `.wide-table-section` | Wrapper of a table (or diagram) on a landscape page. See [Landscape pages](header-footer.md#landscape-pages). |

Tips:

- Do not put `break-inside: avoid` on `table`. A table that does not fit the rest of a page would then jump to the next page and leave a gap. Put it on `tr`: the table breaks between rows and the header row repeats.
- `td, th { overflow-wrap: break-word }` is in the base CSS, so long words wrap.

## Callouts

| Selector | What it is |
| -------- | ---------- |
| `.callout` | Every callout, a `div` (or a `span` with `display: block` for inline callouts). |
| `.callout-<group>` | The style group: `note`, `abstract`, `info`, `todo`, `tip`, `success`, `question`, `warning`, `failure`, `danger`, `bug`, `example`, `quote`. |
| `.callout-<type>` | The type as written, for aliases: `.callout-caution` next to `.callout-warning`. |
| `[data-callout="<type>"]` | The type as written, as attribute. |
| `.callout-title` | The title, a `span` holding a `strong`. |

```css
.callout-warning { background: #fff8e1; border-left-color: #f59e0b; color: #7a4b00; }
.callout-title { text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.03em; }
.callout[data-callout="checklist"] { border-left-color: #2c7a7b; }
```

## Images and diagrams

| Selector | What it is |
| -------- | ---------- |
| `img.doc-image`, `svg.doc-image` | Embedded images. SVG files are inline `svg` elements with the same class. |
| `figure`, `figcaption` | An image with a caption. |
| `figure.pdf-embed`, `img.pdf-embed-page`, `p.pdf-embed-more` | A [PDF embed](../obsidian/embeds.md#pdf): the figure, one image per page and the note about pages left out. The figure may break between pages. A page taller than the text area of a template needs a smaller `max-height` on `img.pdf-embed-page`. |
| `.mermaid`, `.mermaid-<type>` | A rendered [Mermaid](../obsidian/mermaid.md) diagram, such as `.mermaid-flowchart`, `.mermaid-pie`, `.mermaid-gantt`, `.mermaid-sequenceDiagram`. `graph` blocks get `mermaid-flowchart`. The type keeps its case. |
| `.landscape-figure`, `.landscape` | A wide diagram on a landscape page: the wrapper (with `.wide-table-section`) and the diagram. |
| `span.math.inline`, `span.math.display`, `svg.math-svg` | [Math](../markdown/math.md). `.math-source` is a formula that failed and is shown as code. |

### Mermaid diagrams

A rule of the template wins over the size ope sets, because ope gives the size as a rule with zero specificity:

```css
.mermaid-pie   { height: 6cm; width: auto; }
.mermaid-gantt { width: 100%; }
```

A diagram is never wider than the text (`max-width: 100%`). `default` styles images with `img:where(.doc-image)`, so a class rule such as `.mermaid-pie` also wins over its `height: auto`. A template that sets `height` on `img.doc-image` needs a selector that is at least as specific, for example `img.mermaid-pie`.

## Footnotes

Each footnote is a `span.footnote` with `data-footnote-number` at the place of its reference. The base CSS floats it to the footnote area at the bottom of the page:

```css
.footnote { float: footnote; font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1.35; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; }
.footnote::footnote-call { content: attr(data-footnote-number); vertical-align: super; font-size: 0.65rem; line-height: 0; }
.footnote::footnote-marker { content: attr(data-footnote-number) ". "; }
.footnote-paragraph { display: block; }
@page { @footnote { margin-top: 0.8em; padding-top: 0.3em; border-top: 0.5pt solid #999; } }
```

| Selector | What it is |
| -------- | ---------- |
| `.footnote` | The note text, moved to the bottom of the page. |
| `.footnote::footnote-call` | The number in the text. |
| `.footnote::footnote-marker` | The number in front of the note. |
| `@page { @footnote { ... } }` | The footnote area: rule, spacing. |
| `.footnote-paragraph` | Second and later paragraphs of a note. |
| `section.footnotes`, `a.footnote-ref`, `a.footnote-back` | The list of notes at the end, for notes with block content or with `-O footnotes=end`. |

A note takes its style from where it is referenced, so a note referenced in a callout inherits its colour. `default` sets `.footnote { color: var(--color-dark) }`. Use `data-footnote-number`, not `counter(footnote)`: the numbers come from pandoc and run through the whole document, also into the list at the end.

## Redline

| Selector | What it is |
| -------- | ---------- |
| `ins`, `del` | Inserted and removed words inside a changed block. |
| `.redline-ins`, `.redline-del` | Inserted and removed blocks. |

## The base CSS

ope adds this before the template CSS. A template can override any of it.

```css
ul.task-list, ol.task-list { list-style: none; }
ul.task-list > li, ol.task-list > li { list-style: none; }
.task-checkbox { display: inline; margin-right: 0.4em; font-family: "DejaVu Sans", sans-serif; }
span.math.display { display: block; text-align: center; margin: 0.6em 0; }
svg.math-svg { display: inline; overflow: visible; }
.math-source code { white-space: pre-wrap; }
td, th { overflow-wrap: break-word; }
.landscape-figure .landscape { margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; }
figure.pdf-embed { break-inside: auto; page-break-inside: auto; }
img.pdf-embed-page {
  display: block; margin: 0 auto 0.8em; box-sizing: border-box;
  width: auto; height: auto; max-width: 100%; max-height: 22cm;
  border: 0.75pt solid #999; break-inside: avoid;
}
.pdf-embed-more { font-size: 0.85em; color: #666; margin: 0 0 0.3em; }
figure.pdf-embed figcaption { break-before: avoid; page-break-before: avoid; }
```

plus the footnote rules above, and one rule per image width used in the document (`:where(img[width="300"]) { width: 300px; }`), because WeasyPrint ignores the `width` attribute.

## WeasyPrint is not a browser

- Flexbox and grid work only in part. Block layout, simple flex and CSS counters are safe.
- Images cannot be split. An image that does not fit below the current text moves to the next page. Limit its size, for example with `max-height`, to keep it on the page.
- Print media applies: `@media print` rules are used.
- Supported CSS is listed in the [WeasyPrint docs](https://doc.courtbouillon.org/weasyprint/stable/api_reference.html#supported-features).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templating/python/

# Python templates

A Python template can do what a folder cannot: build the header and footer from the title, version or `-O` options, extend a built-in template instead of copying its CSS, and change the Markdown or HTML of the document.

## The `Template` class

```python
from obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates import Decorations, ExportContext, Template

class MyTemplate(Template):
    name = "mytemplate"                  # the --template name, must be unique
    description = "Shown by list-templates"

    def get_css(self) -> str: ...                                   # required in practice
    def assets(self) -> dict[str, bytes]: return {}                 # name -> bytes
    def decorations(self, context: ExportContext) -> Decorations | None: return None
    def mermaid_config(self, context: ExportContext) -> dict[str, object]: return {}
    def process_markdown(self, content: str, context: ExportContext) -> str: return content
    def process_html(self, html: str, context: ExportContext) -> str: return html
```

| Member | Called | Notes |
| ------ | ------ | ----- |
| `name` | | Identifier for `--template`. |
| `description` | | One line for `list-templates`. |
| `get_css()` | Before the export, without context | The CSS source. Written to `<build>/<name>.css`. |
| `assets()` | Before the export | Files written into the build folder, for relative `url(...)` in the CSS. |
| `decorations(ctx)` | After the HTML hooks | Running header and footer HTML and page CSS. `None` for none. |
| `mermaid_config(ctx)` | Before Mermaid runs | Base Mermaid config. `-O mermaid.config` and `-O mermaid.theme` are merged over it. |
| `process_markdown(content, ctx)` | Right before pandoc | The assembled Markdown of the whole document, after all steps and plugins. |
| `process_html(html, ctx)` | After pandoc and the HTML steps | The full HTML document, before decorations. |

One instance is made per export. Do not keep state on the class.

`get_css()` has no context. Anything that depends on the title or `-O` options goes into `decorations`, `process_markdown` or `process_html`.

## `ExportContext`

```python
@dataclass
class ExportContext:
    title: str                 # --title or the folder name
    subtitle: str = ""         # --subtitle
    version: str = ""          # --version (export only)
    date: str = ""             # --date or today, ISO
    label: str = ""            # version, short commit hash, "Redline: a -> b" or empty
    output_path: Path          # the PDF
    build_dir: Path            # the build folder, for scratch files
    options: dict[str, str]    # the -O key=value pairs

    @property
    def formatted_date(self) -> str: ...   # "7 May, 2026" for an ISO date
```

Treat it as read-only.

## `Decorations`

```python
@dataclass
class Decorations:
    running_html: str = ""     # put right after <body>
    page_css: str = ""         # put into <head>
```

The mechanics are described in [Header and footer](header-footer.md). Strings from the context must be escaped: HTML escaping for `running_html`, CSS string escaping for `content: "..."`.

## Extend a built-in template

Subclass `DefaultTemplate` to keep its CSS, header and footer and add to them. This template adds a confidentiality label from `-O confidentiality=...`:

```python title="confidential.py"
"""A template that adds a confidentiality label from ``-O confidentiality=...``.

It extends the built-in default template, so it keeps all of its CSS and
its header and footer, and only adds a label at the top right of each page.

    ope export ./Notes -T confidential -O confidentiality=Internal
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates import Decorations
from obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates import ExportContext
from obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates.builtin.default import DefaultTemplate

class ConfidentialTemplate(DefaultTemplate):
    """The default template plus a confidentiality label."""

    name = "confidential"
    description = "Default template with a confidentiality label"

    def decorations(self, context: ExportContext) -> Decorations | None:
        base = super().decorations(context) or Decorations()
        label = context.options.get("confidentiality", "")
        if not label:
            return base
        escaped = label.replace("&", "&amp;").replace("<", "&lt;")
        running_html = f'<span class="confidential-label">{escaped}</span>\n'
        page_css = """
.confidential-label {
    position: running(confidential);
    font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;
    font-size: 8pt;
    font-weight: bold;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: #c53030;
    border: 1.5pt solid #c53030;
    padding: 2pt 6pt;
}
@page {
    @top-right { content: element(confidential); vertical-align: bottom; padding-bottom: 12pt; }
}
"""
        return Decorations(
            running_html=base.running_html + running_html,
            page_css=base.page_css + page_css,
        )

#: Picked up by scripts/render_examples.py for the docs screenshots.
TEMPLATE = ConfidentialTemplate
```

The result is in the [recipes](recipes.md#confidentiality-label).

## Change Markdown or HTML

Use these hooks only when CSS cannot do it:

```python
def process_markdown(self, content: str, context: ExportContext) -> str:
    if context.options.get("draft") == "yes":
        return "::: {.draft-banner}\nDraft, not approved\n:::\n\n" + content
    return content

def process_html(self, html: str, context: ExportContext) -> str:
    return html.replace('class="title"', 'class="title brand-title"')
```

`process_markdown` gets the Markdown after the steps and plugins: Dataview tables and Meta Bind values are already in place. Decorations are added after `process_html`, so it cannot change them. If the syntax of the notes is the problem, write a [plugin](../plugins/write-a-plugin.md) instead.

## Assets

```python
from importlib import resources
from pathlib import Path

from obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates.base import asset_data_uri

def assets(self) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    return {"logo.svg": (resources.files(__package__) / "logo.svg").read_bytes()}

# For an image in running_html, a data URI avoids WeasyPrint's URL rules in margin boxes:
logo = asset_data_uri(Path(__file__).with_name("logo.svg"))
running_html = f'<img class="brand-logo" src="{logo}">'
```

## Publish as a package

Register the class under the entry point group `obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates`:

```toml title="pyproject.toml"
[project]
name = "acme-pdf-template"
dependencies = ["obsidian-pdf-exporter"]

[project.entry-points."obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates"]
confidential = "acme_pdf_template:ConfidentialTemplate"
```

```bash
uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter --with acme-pdf-template   # or with a local path
ope list-templates
ope export ./Vault -T confidential -O confidentiality=Internal
```

## Register at runtime

When ope is used as a library:

```python
from obsidian_pdf_exporter.main import app
from obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates import register_template

register_template(MyTemplate)               # under MyTemplate.name
register_template(MyTemplate, name="alt")   # or another name
app(["export", "./Vault", "-T", "mytemplate"], standalone_mode=False)
```

Runtime templates win over entry points of the same name. This is how the docs screenshots of the confidentiality recipe are made, see `scripts/render_examples.py`.

## Options

`-O key=value` reaches the template as `context.options`. By convention a template uses `<template>.<key>` for its own options and a bare key for options shared with plugins.

A template is Python code and can do anything Python can. Review third-party templates like any other dependency.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templating/recipes/

# Recipes

Each recipe is a complete template in [`examples/_templates/`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/tree/main/examples/_templates). The pictures show the same sample page with the `default` template (left) and with the recipe (right), exported with:

```bash
ope export ./Handbook --title "Team handbook" --version 1.2.0 --date 2026-04-01 --no-toc -T <recipe>
```

The folder recipes keep only the rules they add in `custom.css`. To use one, put a copy of [`default.css`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/templates/builtin/default/default.css) into the folder as `main.css` and append `custom.css` to it:

```bash
cp -r examples/_templates/letterhead examples/_templates/assets ~/.config/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templates/
cd ~/.config/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templates/letterhead
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/templates/builtin/default/default.css > main.css
cat custom.css >> main.css && rm custom.css
ope export ./Handbook -T letterhead
```

## Company letterhead

A logo at the top right of every page, the address on the first page, the document title on the following pages, and a teal accent colour.

![Before: default template](../img/templates/default.png)
![After: letterhead](../img/templates/letterhead.png)

=== "template.yaml"

    ```yaml
    name: letterhead
    description: Logo on every page, address on the first page
    css: main.css
    running_html: header.html
    page_css: page.css
    ```

=== "header.html"

    ```html
    <img class="letterhead-logo" src="../assets/logo.svg" alt="Example Ltd.">
    <div class="letterhead-address">Example Ltd. · 1 Sample Street · 12345 Sample City · www.example.com</div>
    ```

=== "page.css"

    ```css
    /* Running elements: taken out of the text and placed in margin boxes. */
    .letterhead-logo { position: running(logo); width: 40mm; }
    .letterhead-address { position: running(address); font-size: 7pt; color: #606872; }

    /* The document title from the title block, for the header of later pages. */
    header#title-block-header .title { string-set: doc-title content(); }

    @page {
      margin: 30mm 20mm 22mm 20mm;
      @top-left { content: string(doc-title); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 8pt; font-weight: bold; vertical-align: bottom; padding-bottom: 10pt; }
      @top-right { content: element(logo); vertical-align: bottom; padding-bottom: 6pt; }
      @bottom-right { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; content: "Page " counter(page) " / " counter(pages); font-size: 7pt; color: #606872; }
    }

    /* First page: address instead of the title, and more room for the letterhead. */
    @page :first {
      margin-top: 40mm;
      @top-left { content: element(address); vertical-align: bottom; padding-bottom: 10pt; }
    }
    ```

=== "custom.css"

    ```css
    /* Accent colour taken from the logo. */
    :root { --color-accent: #2c7a7b; }
    ```

The logo is `../assets/logo.svg`, a [shared asset](folders.md#sharing-assets-between-templates). It becomes a data URI when the template is loaded, so it shows inside the margin box.

## Change the footer text

Title and version line at the bottom left, a fixed notice in the middle, "Page X of Y" at the right. The header is left out. This recipe changes only `page.css`, so `main.css` is an unchanged copy of `default.css`.

![Before: default template](../img/templates/default.png)
![After: footer text](../img/templates/footer-text.png)

=== "template.yaml"

    ```yaml
    name: footer-text
    description: Title, version and page count in the footer
    css: main.css
    page_css: page.css
    ```

=== "page.css"

    ```css
    /* Copy the title and the version line of the title block into named strings. */
    header#title-block-header .title { string-set: doc-title content(); }
    header#title-block-header .author { string-set: doc-meta content(); }

    @page {
      @bottom-left { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; content: string(doc-title) " · " string(doc-meta); font-size: 7pt; color: #606872; }
      @bottom-center { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; content: "Internal draft, do not forward"; font-size: 7pt; color: #c53030; }
      @bottom-right { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; content: "Page " counter(page) " of " counter(pages); font-size: 7pt; color: #606872; }
    }
    ```

## Confidentiality label

A label at the top right, set per export with `-O confidentiality=Internal`. The text comes from an option, so this is a [Python template](python.md). It extends `default` and keeps everything else.

![Before: default template](../img/templates/default.png)
![After: confidentiality label](../img/templates/confidential.png)

```python title="confidential.py"
"""A template that adds a confidentiality label from ``-O confidentiality=...``.

It extends the built-in default template, so it keeps all of its CSS and
its header and footer, and only adds a label at the top right of each page.

    ope export ./Notes -T confidential -O confidentiality=Internal
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates import Decorations
from obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates import ExportContext
from obsidian_pdf_exporter.templates.builtin.default import DefaultTemplate

class ConfidentialTemplate(DefaultTemplate):
    """The default template plus a confidentiality label."""

    name = "confidential"
    description = "Default template with a confidentiality label"

    def decorations(self, context: ExportContext) -> Decorations | None:
        base = super().decorations(context) or Decorations()
        label = context.options.get("confidentiality", "")
        if not label:
            return base
        escaped = label.replace("&", "&amp;").replace("<", "&lt;")
        running_html = f'<span class="confidential-label">{escaped}</span>\n'
        page_css = """
.confidential-label {
    position: running(confidential);
    font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;
    font-size: 8pt;
    font-weight: bold;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: #c53030;
    border: 1.5pt solid #c53030;
    padding: 2pt 6pt;
}
@page {
    @top-right { content: element(confidential); vertical-align: bottom; padding-bottom: 12pt; }
}
"""
        return Decorations(
            running_html=base.running_html + running_html,
            page_css=base.page_css + page_css,
        )

#: Picked up by scripts/render_examples.py for the docs screenshots.
TEMPLATE = ConfidentialTemplate
```

Register it as an entry point (see [Publish as a package](python.md#publish-as-a-package)) and export with:

```bash
ope export ./Handbook -T confidential -O confidentiality=Internal
```

For a fixed label, a folder template is enough: put `@top-right { content: "INTERNAL"; }` into its `page.css`.

## Compact variant

Smaller text, tighter spacing and narrow margins, for long reference documents.

![Before: default template](../img/templates/default.png)
![After: compact](../img/templates/compact.png)

=== "custom.css"

    ```css
    html { font-size: 10pt; }
    body { line-height: 1.35; }
    @page { margin: 14mm 14mm 16mm 14mm; }
    @page landscape-page { margin: 14mm; }
    h1, h2, h3, h4 { margin-top: 0.9em; margin-bottom: 0.3em; }
    p { margin-bottom: 0.45em; }
    th, td { padding: 3px 6px; }
    .callout { padding: 6px 10px; margin: 0.6em 0; }
    ```

=== "page.css"

    ```css
    header#title-block-header .title { string-set: doc-title content(); }
    @page {
      @top-left { content: string(doc-title); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 7pt; font-weight: bold; vertical-align: bottom; padding-bottom: 6pt; }
      @bottom-right { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; content: counter(page) " / " counter(pages); font-size: 7pt; color: #606872; }
    }
    ```

=== "template.yaml"

    ```yaml
    name: compact
    description: Smaller text and margins
    css: main.css
    page_css: page.css
    ```

## Dark variant

Light text on a dark page, for reading on screens. Most of it is a change of the [colour variables](css-reference.md#colour-and-font-variables-of-default).

![Before: default template](../img/templates/default.png)
![After: dark](../img/templates/dark.png)

=== "custom.css"

    ```css
    :root {
      --color-accent: #90cdf4;
      --color-grey: #a0aec0;
      --color-light-grey: #2d3748;
      --color-mid-grey: #4a5568;
      --color-dark: #edf2f7;
    }
    @page { background: #1a202c; }
    @page landscape-page { background: #1a202c; }
    body { background: transparent; color: var(--color-dark); }
    thead tr { background: #2c5282; }
    th { color: #ffffff; }
    td { border-color: var(--color-mid-grey); }
    code, pre { background: #2d3748; color: #edf2f7; }
    .callout { background: #2d3748; }
    .callout, .callout * { color: var(--color-dark); }
    ```

=== "page.css"

    ```css
    header#title-block-header .title { string-set: doc-title content(); }
    @page {
      @top-left { content: string(doc-title); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 7pt; font-weight: bold; color: #edf2f7; vertical-align: bottom; padding-bottom: 6pt; }
      @bottom-right { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; content: counter(page) " / " counter(pages); font-size: 7pt; color: #a0aec0; }
    }
    ```

`@page { background: ... }` colours the whole sheet, margins included. `body` alone would leave a white border.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/templating/debugging/

# Debugging

## Keep the build folder

```bash
ope export ./Vault --debug -o out/handbook.pdf
```

The build folder stays next to the PDF and is named after it, here `out/_build_handbook/`:

| File | What it is |
| ---- | ---------- |
| `assembled.md` | The Markdown pandoc reads: all pages after the steps, plugins and `process_markdown`. |
| `output.html` | The HTML pandoc wrote. |
| `final.html` | The HTML WeasyPrint lays out: after the HTML steps, `process_html`, the header and footer HTML and the page CSS. |
| `<template>.css` | The template CSS. |
| images, diagrams | Copied and rendered images, assets of the template. |

## Find where something goes wrong

1. The text is wrong or missing: look at `assembled.md`. If the syntax is still there unchanged, no step or plugin handled it. Check the `Warning:` lines of the export.
2. The structure is wrong (a list is a paragraph, a table is text): pandoc read the Markdown differently. Run pandoc on `assembled.md` by hand to try changes.
3. Only the look is wrong: look at `final.html` and the CSS.

## Open final.html in a browser

```bash
xdg-open out/_build_handbook/final.html    # Linux
open out/_build_handbook/final.html        # macOS
start out\_build_handbook\final.html       # Windows
```

The browser's developer tools show which rules apply to an element and which classes it has. A browser does not draw `@page` margin boxes, running elements or footnote areas, and it lays out some things differently from WeasyPrint. Use it to check selectors, not page breaks.

To check page layout, run WeasyPrint on the file directly:

```bash
uv tool run weasyprint out/_build_handbook/final.html test.pdf
```

WeasyPrint prints a warning for each CSS rule it ignores, with the line of the CSS, for example `Ignored 'gap: 1em' at 4:28, invalid value`.

## Check the PDF from the command line

```bash
pdftotext -layout handbook.pdf - | less                    # the text, for searching and diffs
pdftoppm -r 80 -png -f 1 -l 3 handbook.pdf page            # the first three pages as page-1.png ...
pdfinfo handbook.pdf                                        # page count and page size
```

`pdftotext`, `pdftoppm` and `pdfinfo` are part of poppler (`poppler-utils` on Debian and Ubuntu).

## Common problems

| Problem | Cause and fix |
| ------- | ------------- |
| `Multiple CSS files in ...` | A template folder has more than one CSS file. Set `css:` in `template.yaml`. |
| The header and footer are gone | A folder or single-file template replaces `default` completely, header and footer included. Add them in `page.css`, see [Header and footer](header-footer.md). |
| A logo in the header does not show | The image is not an asset of the template, or the path in `src` differs from the asset name. Assets are matched by their exact path, such as `logo.svg` or `../assets/logo.svg`. |
| A `content: "..."` rule breaks the CSS | A quote or backslash in the text is not escaped. |
| Wide tables have other margins | The template changed `@page` but not `@page landscape-page`. |
| A table leaves a big gap | `break-inside: avoid` is set on `table`. Put it on `tr`. |
| An image jumps to the next page | Images cannot be split. Limit the size with `max-height`. |
| Mermaid blocks stay code | Neither `mmdc` nor `npx` was found. Install Node.js or mermaid-cli. |
